title: "Can we make sure the model information is being pased through accurately ![image.png](assets/image.png) We seem to have some sort of regression when moving to the runner architecture where we are reporting default for model constantly. And like in this case reporting a model that isnt in use as its a CI stage I want the runner to be able to accurately report (through the backend) to the ui what model choices etc it is running. And I want to make sure the general model catalogue behaviours work."

# Goal
# Can we make sure the model information is being pased through accurately

![image.png](assets/image.png)

We seem to have some sort of regression when moving to the runner architecture where we are reporting default for model constantly. And like in this case reporting a model that isnt in use as its a CI stage

I want the runner to be able to accurately report (through the backend) to the ui what model choices etc it is running. And I want to make sure the general model catalogue behaviours work.

User understandable over technical language 4| 5|I feel like code should always be understandable by users as they are the ones who dictate process. So the goal of code should make it the most understandable with zero context as possible 6| 7|### Principles 8| 9|- Long variables names where needed to be descriptive 10|- Avoid using technical language such as “factory” or “barrel” 11|- Stick to a common language profile, (tasks always being tasks, stages always being stages etc) 12|- File structure should reflect the call stack…","meta":{"toolName":"read_file","toolCallId":"call_01a197fde90c76b79ce3cdeb21ee9843","source":"runner-structured","runnerId":"local-alpha","executionId":"ac0d91e0-5b2d-4e3b-b6cc-3c37a9e716e9","seq":6},"fidelity":"normalized","seq":15,"tool":{"callId":"call_01a197fde90c76b79ce3cdeb21ee9843","name":"read_file","result":"Read text file `docs/KB Code Standards.md`.\n1|# Values\n2|\n3|## User understandable over technical language\n4|\n5|I feel like code should always be understandable by users as they are the ones who dictate process. So the goal of code should make it the most understandable with zero context as possible\n6|\n7|### Principles\n8|\n9|- Long variables names where needed to be descriptive\n10|- Avoid using technical language such as “factory” or “barrel”\n11|- Stick to a common language profile, (tasks always being tasks, stages always being stages etc)\n12|- File structure should reflect the call stack\n13|- Use of JSDocs to explain variables in pure english\n14|- Include why things are done not just what is done\n15|- Use a labelled data inport pattern (IE  `({varA , varB}) => {}`)\n16|- NEVER MENTION DESIGN PATTERNS\n17|- Use @example tags in js doc to easily explain functionality\n18|  \n19|  \n20|\n21|## Functional over Object oreintated\n22|\n23|Although pure functional code can tend to insanity it is always important to note co-mingle state and functionality. Where possible state should leave in clearly defined places, and functions should show a clear line in how we move from one state to another. Traditional object oriented design mainly serves to gatekeep devs(or for game dev).\n24|\n25|### Principles\n26|\n27|- Try and avoid using classes where possible\n28|- Currying can be used to create sudo classes, avoid that\n29|- Functions should follow black box mentality, clear input delivers the same output with no side affects\n30|- Treat variables as immutable unless they are clearly defined states.\n31|- Functions should always be named with a verb in, as they are doing something\n32|- Give the miniumn data to each function as possible. Pick off fields before invocation.\n33|- Each function should only work to achieve its task, with a single responsibility\n34|\n35|\n36|## Co-location over abstraction\n37|\n38|Although abstraction is an essential part of coding it should always only be done by business level intent, not just on functionality. Ideally if you pick a random file in the codebase you should only need to look at the one folder above it and one folder under it to get all the context on its functionality.\n39|\n40|### Principles\n41|- Unit tests should always be placed next to the relevant file\n42|- Generally functions called in a higher function should be placed in a folder of that functions name. IE if `funA.js` calls `funB.js` it should be `./funA/funB.js`\n43|- Generic/helper functions should only be made if they are repeatedly doing the same thing.\n44|- Helpers should be treated like react state and exist at the lowest level folder that is common in the hierarchy of the folders\n45|- If abstracting it would take up more lines/characters than just embedding that line directly on a per file basis avoid doing it. IE don’t abstract a single line just because its repeated unless it has some complex logic like a regex.\n46|- Don’t fear repetition of code\n47|- Make sure the code is easily searchable for any given task. If I said modify the task history box in the ui it should  be easy and logical to figure out where that is.\n48|- Use folders as a tool for organising\n49|\n50|## Tested over trusted \n51|\n52|Functionality should not assumed to exist until it is tested and evidenced. “it should work” isn’t always reliable and we want to make sure there are no regressions. \n53|\n54|### Principles\n55|- Try and at least plan what tests you are going to make before you  code a function\n56|- Don’t assume typing is correct until proven, or allow it to fail safe\n57|- Failures should clear transparent and observable, every function doesnt need to intensly check it just needs to report failures accurately\n58|- Tests must be consistent\n59|- Integration test must reflect how a user could want to use the app\n60|- Use the lowest possible level of tests( Ie Unit over api over e2e) for the fastest test cycle\n61|\n62|\n63|## Fast iteration over long planning\n64|\n65|Sometimes you just can’t know what will happen without using it and that is essential. Spending too long planning can cause ideas to get confused or get you trapped in a loop where you just make plans worse.  Having simple clear checkpoints is great.\n66|\n67|### Principles\n68|- When planning, factor in points to check certain things and how the plan can be adapted when needed\n69|- Try and create safe ways to test functionality, ie not in prod, when possible as this will allow you to confirm things work.\n70|- Focus on one small change at a time, get tests passing then work on the next element.\n71|- Always design code with the intent it will be changed/replaced soon\n72|- Minimise friction in development even if it is small\n73|- Make change easy, then make the change. Even if making change easy is hard.\n74|\n75|\n76|\n77|# Inspirations\n78|My principles here are inspired by:\n79|\n80|- Extreme programming Explained by Kent Beck (book)\n81|- Life isn’t binary (book)\n82|- Intent driven design by David whitney (Talk)\n83|\n84|\n85|# Examples\n86|\n87|## Intent Driven descriptions\n88|\n89|### Bad Example\n90|\n91|```js\n92|\n93|const userInOneYearFactory = (name, age, users) => {\n94|\n95|    const user = {name: name , age: age + 1}\n96|\n97|    users.push(user)\n98|  \n99|}\n100|\n101|const list = []\n102|\n103|userFactory(\"Frank\",32,list)\n104|\n105|\n106|```\n107|\n108|## Good example\n109|\n110|```js\n111|\n112|/**\n113|* MARK: calculateAgeNextYear\n114|* @description calculates the age someone will be next year\n115|* @example const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: 3})  \n116|console.log(usersAgeNextYear) // 4\n117|*/\n118|const calculateAgeNextYear = ({ageNow}) => {\n119|  const ageNextYear = ageNow + 1\n120|  \n121|  return ageNextYear\n122|}\n123|\n124|const userObjectsList = []\n125|\n126|const usersName = \"Frank\"\n127|const usersAge = 32\n128|\n129|const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: usersAge})\n130|\n131|userObjectsList.push({name: usersName, age: usersAge})\n132|\n133|\n134|```"}},{"id":16,"ts":"2026-11-01T16:42:43.532Z","feed":"tools","feeds":["tools"],"kind":"tool","turn":1,"text":"[RESULT] Read text file `docs/tasks/e3b2624a-bc24-4698-9c78-86af7f6f3b5b/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`. 1|# Implementation Plan: Accurate Model Information Passthrough 2| 3|> **Task:** Fix Runner → backend → UI model reporting so the UI shows the actual served model for agent stages, nothing for CI stages, and the model catalogue behaves correctly. 4|> **Survey basis:** `SURVEY.md` — all questions answered with recommended options; see §1. 5|> **Principle:** Make change easy, then make the change. 6| 7|--- 8| 9|## 1. Survey Decisions (Locked)\n10|\n11|| # | Question | Answer |\n12||---|----------|--------|\n13|| Q1 | Agent stage model in UI | Only the actual model the Runner serves (not the Runner default) |\n14|| Q2 | CI stage model field | No model / blank (CI uses no LLM) |\n15|| Q3 | Model source for reporting + dispatch | The exact model required by the dispatched task (`requirements.model`) |\n16|| Q4 | Task requires model Runner didn't advertise | Refuse assignment (leave for another Runner); alias: check other targets |\n17|| Q5 | Catalogue behaviours that must keep working | All five: picker non-empty, harness-specific lists correct, runnable/auth labels accurate, aliases resolve, dispatch matches available models |\n18|| Q6 | Model/harness pill while running (Runners view) | Yes, always while running |\n19|\n20|**Derived invariants:**\n21|\n22|- `config.model` / `config.models` is the Runner's **advertised capability** (what it _can_ run). It keeps the smallest focused test with the delivered project and updates coverage when behavior changes. Adding features to a project created earlier in this session is greenfield work, not a behavior change; a report that something already built behaves wrongly is still a bug fix. Do not load for greenfield work unless reusable tests are explicitly required, behavior-preserving refactors, verification-only work, plan/review/explanation/documentation/formatting/generated-output-only work, explicit no-change or no-tool work, or when the user declines tests.\nuser-invocable: false\n---\n\n# Durable Test Collateral\n\nVerification is part of the delivered project when it can prevent the same\nbehavior from breaking again. Use the project&apos;s existing framework and\nconventions.\n\nLoading this skill does not mean the current turn asked for the change. While you\nare still investigating — explaining existing behavior, or answering a design\nquestion the user raised — use commands that only read and leave the repository\nunmodified, tests included.\n\n## Scale to the task\n\nSkip the failing-test-first workflow below when the change is tiny and leaves\nprogram logic alone (a typo, a text or style tweak, a config value, or a version\npin), when the work is a throwaway prototype or a standalone one-file script or\npage, when the request adds features to a project you created earlier in this\nsession, or when the user asks for speed or a quick result. A quick direct check\nof the changed behavior is enough there; if you add no maintained test, say so in\nthe report. A user request for tests anywhere in the session, or a\nspecification that makes tests a deliverable, still applies.\n\nAny other bug fix or behavior change keeps the workflow at its smallest: one\nfocused failing test, the fix, that test passing, and, when a broad run is\nrequired, one broad run after the final edit. A report that something already\nbuilt behaves wrongly is a bug fix, even when it comes with feature requests.\n\nBefore a test run that may take more than a minute or two, tell the user in one\nline what runs and why. If you poll it, post a short status line between polls;\nnever poll a long run silently.\n\n## Keep the check with the project\n\nFor a bug fix or behavior change, add or update the smallest maintained test in\nthe repository&apos;s normal test layout that exercises the changed behavior. If a\nspecification makes a reusable suite or test category a deliverable, implement\nthat suite instead of treating it as private verification.\n\nAn inline interpreter command, heredoc, scratch script, temporary-directory\ntest, demo, or manual probe may help diagnose the problem, but it does not\nreplace the maintained test. Keep a useful self-authored test where the project\nkeeps its tests. If there is no such place, or the request restricts what the\ndelivered directory may contain, put the test outside that directory (for\nexample under `/tmp`) and name it in the report.\n\nDo not add a new test framework solely to satisfy this skill. If the repository\nhas no maintained harness and the request does not require one, disclose when\ndurable coverage would be disproportionate or infeasible and use the narrowest\nhonest verification instead.\n\nOn a later turn, update the maintained test even when the old suite remains\ngreen and the user does not repeat the test request. Cover the new behavior,\nnot merely an unrelated cleanup in the test file.\n\n## Aim the check where it can fail\n\nAssert what the request requires, not what you built, and end every probe in\nan assertion. If a probe shows a result the request forbids, fix the code, not\nthe assertion. Any input the public interface allows is in scope. If the\nrequest says the code may do something, that is allowed, not required.\n\nBug classes a happy-path check misses:\n\n- Ordering: when results must be acknowledged or shown in order, test with\n  items that finish out of order, and check that nothing is acknowledged or\n  shown before the items ahead of it.\n- Untrusted input: a sanitizer or filter must fail closed. If any step errors,\n  output nothing or escaped text, never the raw input.\n\n## Test the transition\n\nWhen a write can stay pending while a background step rewrites or cleans up\nstate, test reads while writes are still pending during that step, not only\nafter everything settles. A read that contradicts the request is a bug to fix.\n\n## Prove the maintained check\n\nObserve the authentic failure before the implementation change when it is safe\nand runnable. Then make the smallest implementation change and run the focused\nmaintained test after the final relevant source or test edit.\n\nDo not weaken or delete a real failing test to obtain green. Fix the product,\nor explain why the test&apos;s expectation is wrong before changing that\nexpectation. Do not repeat an unchanged check solely to collect evidence.\n\nRun a broad or full suite only when the user, a repository gate, or\nproportionate risk requires it, and then once, after the final edit, rather\nthan after each intermediate edit. A focused regression test comes first; broad\nproof does not substitute for missing focused coverage.\n\nBefore deciding what a repository gate requires, read what the repository\ndeclares it runs: its CI workflow, its test entry points, and its root-level\nscripts listed with hidden entries included. A suite the project itself runs\nover this change is a gate, not an optional extra, and a suite that skips\nitself when its data is absent is not a green result.\n\nA runner is unavailable only after you tried to make it available. A report that something already\nbuilt behaves wrongly is a bug fix, even when it comes with feature requests.\n\nBefore a test run that may take more than a minute or two, tell the user in one\nline what runs and why. If you poll it, post a short status line between polls;\nnever poll a long run silently.\n\n## Keep the check with the project\n\nFor a bug fix or behavior change, add or update the smallest maintained test in\nthe repository&apos;s normal test layout that exercises the changed behavior. If a\nspecification makes a reusable suite or test category a deliverable, implement\nthat suite instead of treating it as private verification.\n\nAn inline interpreter command, heredoc, scratch script, temporary-directory\ntest, demo, or manual probe may help diagnose the problem, but it does not\nreplace the maintained test. New Runners already omit the model segment for non-LLM\\n *   stages (see…)","meta":{"toolName":"write_file","toolCallId":"call_01a197ff337c7100b9c92db1a116073b","args":"{\"path\":\"shared/cleanReportedPosture.js\",\"content\":\"/***\\n * MARK: cleanReportedPosture\\n * @description Cleans a posture string exactly as it arrives from a\\n *   Runner, so Runners older than the served-model fix cannot leak the\\n *   fake model segment into the stored history during a mixed-version\\n *   rollout. New Runners already omit the model segment for non-LLM\\n *   stages (see `formatPosture`), but the backend must not trust that:\\n *   it is the last place the string is stored.\\n *\\n *   Rules:\\n *   1. A non-string, blank, or whitespace-only posture is absent (`null`).\\n *   2. A trailing `:default` segment (any letter case) is dropped, and\\n *      repeated if a hand-built Runner stacked it. The `\\\"default\\\"`\\n *      sentinel means \\\"harness-managed, no pinned model\\\", never a model\\n *      that ran, so it must never be stored as one.\\n *   3. Powers the UI's one-click\n *   \"make the rows add to 100%\" helper; the API never auto-fixes splits\n *   (a non-100 payload is refused so the user sees the correction).\n * @example normalizeTargetPercents([{ harness: \"a\", model: \"m\" }, { harness: \"b\", model: \"n\" }]) => [{ harness: \"a\", model: \"m\", percent: 50 }, { harness: \"b\", model: \"n\", percent: 50 }]\n * @param {unknown} targets - Target rows (harness + model read, percent ignored).\n * @returns {Array<{harness: string, model: string, percent: number}>} Rows summing to exactly 100 (empty when input is empty).\n ***/\nexport function normalizeTargetPercents(targets) {\n\tconst rows = Array.isArray(targets)\n\t\t? targets\n\t\t\t\t.filter((t) => t && typeof t === \"object\" && !Array.isArray(t))\n\t\t\t\t.map((t) => ({\n\t\t\t\t\tharness: typeof t.harness === \"string\" ? t.harness.trim() : \"\",\n\t\t\t\t\tmodel: typeof t.model === \"string\" ? t.model : \"\",\n\t\t\t\t}))\n\t\t: [];\n\tif (rows.length === 0) return [];\n\tconst base = Math.floor(100 / rows.length);\n\tlet leftover = 100 - base * rows.length;\n\treturn rows.map((row) => {\n\t\tconst extra = leftover > 0 ? 1 : 0;\n\t\tleftover -= extra;\n\t\treturn { ...row, percent: base + extra };\n\t});\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: selectWeightedIndex\n * @description ONE deterministic step of smooth weighted round-robin: adds\n *   each weight to its running score, picks the highest scorer (lowest\n *   index wins ties), then subtracts the weight total from the winner so\n *   the next pick rotates. Used by the settings UI to\n *   show impact (\"3 stages use this alias\") and to prove rename migration.\n * @example findAliasUsages(project, \"small\") => { stages: [{ workflowId, stageId, stageName }], usesAsDefault: true }\n * @param {Object} [project] - Project entity.\n * @param {unknown} name - Alias name.\n * @returns {{stages: Array<Object>, usesAsDefault: boolean}} Usage locations.\n ***/\nexport function findAliasUsages(project, name) {\n\tconst wanted = normalizeAliasName(name);\n\tconst usages = { stages: [], usesAsDefault: false };\n\tif (!wanted || !project || typeof project !== \"object\") return usages;\n\tif (\n\t\tisAliasRef(project.harness, project.defaultModel) &&\n\t\tnormalizeAliasName(project.defaultModel) === wanted\n\t) {\n\t\tusages.usesAsDefault = true;\n\t}\n\tconst checkStage = (workflowId, stage) => {\n\t\tif (!stage || typeof stage !== \"object\") return;\n\t\tif (\n\t\t\tisAliasRef(stage.harness, stage.model) &&\n\t\t\tnormalizeAliasName(stage.model) === wanted\n\t\t) {\n\t\t\tusages.stages.push({\n\t\t\t\tworkflowId: workflowId || null,\n\t\t\t\tstageId: stage.id ?? null,\n\t\t\t\tstageName: stage.name ?? null,\n\t\t\t});\n\t\t}\n\t};\n\tif (Array.isArray(project.workflows) && project.workflows.length > 0) {\n\t\t// Named workflows are authoritative (the legacy root list mirrors the\n\t\t// active workflow's stages as copies — scanning both double-counts).\n\t\tfor (const wf of project.workflows) {\n\t\t\tif (!wf || typeof wf !== \"object\") continue;\n\t\t\tfor (const stage of wf.stages || []) checkStage(wf.id, stage);\n\t\t}\n\t} else if (Array.isArray(project.stages)) {\n\t\tfor (const stage of project.stages) checkStage(null, stage);\n\t}\n\treturn usages;\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: applyAliasRename\n * @description Migrates every reference to an alias in place (project default\n *   + all workflow stages + legacy root stages) so a rename can never orphan\n *   stages. Only exact alias references move — stages on other harnesses\n *   whose model merely equals the name are untouched.\n * @example applyAliasRename(project, \"small\", \"medium\") => 3\n * @param {Object} project - Project entity (mutated).\n * @param {unknown} oldName - Current alias name.\n * @param {unknown} newName - Replacement alias name.\n * @returns {number} Count of migrated references.\n ***/\nexport function applyAliasRename(project, oldName, newName) {\n\tconst from = normalizeAliasName(oldName);\n\tconst to = normalizeAliasName(newName);\n\tif (!project || typeof project !== \"object\" || !from || !to || from === to) {\n\t\treturn 0;\n\t}\n\tlet migrated = 0;\n\t// The project default stores its model in `defaultModel` (not `model`).\n\tif (\n\t\tisAliasRef(project.harness, project.defaultModel) &&\n\t\tnormalizeAliasName(project.defaultModel) === from\n\t) {\n\t\tproject.defaultModel = to;\n\t\tmigrated += 1;\n\t}\n\tconst migrateStages = (stages) => {\n\t\tif (!Array.isArray(stages)) return;\n\t\tfor (const stage of stages) {\n\t\t\tif (\n\t\t\t\tstage &&\n\t\t\t\ttypeof stage === \"object\" &&\n\t\t\t\tisAliasRef(stage.harness, stage.model) &&\n\t\t\t\tnormalizeAliasName(stage.model) === from\n\t\t\t) {\n\t\t\t\tstage.model = to;\n\t\t\t\tmigrated += 1;\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t};\n\tif (Array.isArray(project.workflows) && project.workflows.length > 0) {\n\t\t// Named workflows are authoritative (see findAliasUsages).\n\t\tfor (const wf of project.workflows) {\n\t\t\tif (wf && typeof wf === \"object\") migrateStages(wf.stages);\n\t\t}\n\t} else {\n\t\tmigrateStages(project.stages);\n\t}\n\treturn migrated;\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: aliasPseudoModels\n * @description Projects a project's aliases onto catalogue-shaped pseudo-models\n *   (`{ id, name, provider: \"alias\", key, harness: \"alias\" }`) for the virtual\n *   `alias` entry of the harness-first picker. Keys ARE the alias names, so\n *   the picker's exact-key matching, bare-name fallback, and provider\n *   grouping all work with zero picker forks.\n * @example aliasPseudoModels([{ name: \"small\", harness: \"pi\", model: \"m\" }]) => [{ id: \"small\", name: \"small\", provider: \"alias\", key: \"small\", harness: \"alias\" }]\n * @param {unknown} aliases - Alias records (any shape — normalized first).\n * @returns {Array<Object>} Pseudo-model rows (possibly empty).\n ***/\nexport function aliasPseudoModels(aliases) {\n\treturn normalizeModelAliases(aliases).map((a) => ({\n\t\tid: a.name,\n\t\tname: a.name,\n\t\tprovider: ALIAS_HARNESS_ID,\n\t\tkey: a.name,\n\t\tharness: ALIAS_HARNESS_ID,\n\t}));\n}\n","isError":false,"durationMs":2,"source":"runner-structured","runnerId":"local-alpha","executionId":"6156eb89-ccbb-4d4d-9504-237933179721","seq":15},"fidelity":"normalized","seq":35,"blockId":"b10","tool":{"callId":"call_1ikbgluo","name":"read","args":{"path":"shared/modelAliases.js","limit":2000},"result":"/***\n * MARK: modelAliases (shared alias grammar)\n * @description THE single implementation of the KainBain per-project model\n *   alias system, shared verbatim by the backend engine (`api/projectStore.js`,\n *   `api/agentRunner.js`, `api/sessionStore.js`) and the frontend settings UI\n *   (`frontend/src/components/settings/ModelAliasesSection.jsx`) so validation\n *   and resolution rules cannot drift. Plain ESM, zero dependencies.\n *\n *   An alias binds a short per-project name (e.g. `small`, `design`) to one\n *   or more weighted harness + model targets\n *   (`{ name, targets: [{ harness, model, percent }] }`, persisted on\n *   `project.modelAliases`; a legacy `{ name, harness, model }` record reads\n *   as one 100% target). Stages reference aliases through the\n *   existing harness-first fields — `harness: \"alias\"` + `model: \"<name>\"` —\n *   so every inherit/override path keeps working unchanged, and editing an\n *   alias changes every referencing stage with no stage edits (stages store\n *   the reference, never a copy of the concrete values).\n *\n *   `alias` is a VIRTUAL harness id: it never names a real AgentHarness\n *   (registering it throws — see `api/agent/harnessRegistry.js`), and an\n *   alias target pointing back at `alias` is a loop, treated as unknown.\n ***/\n\n/** The virtual harness id that scopes alias references. Never a real harness. */\nexport const ALIAS_HARNESS_ID = \"alias\";\n\n/** Alias names mirror the harness-id shape: lowercase, URL-safe. */\nexport const ALIAS_NAME_PATTERN = /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$/;\n\n/** Maximum alias name length (keeps picker labels and logs readable). */\nexport const ALIAS_NAME_MAX_LENGTH = 64;\n\n/***\n * MARK: normalizeAliasName\n * @description Trims an alias name to its usable form (\"\" when blank or\n *   non-string, i.e. \"no alias named\").\n * @example normalizeAliasName(\"  Small  \") => \"Small\"\n * @example normalizeAliasName(\"\") => \"\"\n * @param {unknown} name - Raw alias name.\n * @returns {string} Trimmed name, or \"\" when unset.\n ***/\nexport function normalizeAliasName(name) {\n\treturn typeof name === \"string\" ? name.trim() : \"\";\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: validateAliasName\n * @description Validates an alias name, returning an error string or null.\n *   Names are trimmed, 1–64 chars, and must match `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*`\n *   (case-sensitive: `Small` and `small` are different aliases, and uppercase\n *   is rejected so references cannot drift by case).\n * @example validateAliasName(\"small\") => null\n * @example validateAliasName(\"Small\") => \"…\"\n * @param {unknown} name - Raw alias name.\n * @returns {string|null} Error message, or null when valid.\n ***/\nexport function validateAliasName(name) {\n\tconst trimmed = normalizeAliasName(name);\n\tif (!trimmed) return \"Alias name is required\";\n\tif (trimmed.length > ALIAS_NAME_MAX_LENGTH) {\n\t\treturn `Alias name must be at most ${ALIAS_NAME_MAX_LENGTH} characters`;\n\t}\n\tif (!ALIAS_NAME_PATTERN.test(trimmed)) {\n\t\treturn \"Alias name must start with a letter or digit and contain only lowercase letters, digits, - and _\";\n\t}\n\treturn null;\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: validateAliasTarget\n * @description Validates ONE weighted target inside a multi-target alias,\n *   returning an error string or null. The target harness must be a\n *   non-empty string that is NOT the virtual `alias` id (loop guard). The\n *   target model is a string in any accepted model-key form (blank is\n *   allowed at the grammar level for self-managed `none` harnesses — the\n *   settings UI additionally requires a model for `list` harnesses). The\n *   percent is an integer 1–100 (the rows of one alias must sum to exactly\n *   100 — see `validateAliasTargets`).\n * @example validateAliasTarget({ harness: \"pi\", model: \"google::m\", percent: 90 }, \"small\") => null\n * @example validateAliasTarget({ harness: \"pi\", model: \"m\", percent: 0 }, \"small\") => \"…\"\n * @param {unknown} target - Candidate `{ harness, model, percent }` record.\n * @param {unknown} aliasName - Owning alias name (for error messages).\n * @returns {string|null} Error message, or null when valid.\n ***/\nexport function validateAliasTarget(target, aliasName) {\n\tconst label =\n\t\tnormalizeAliasName(aliasName) || \"(unnamed alias)\";\n\tif (!target || typeof target !== \"object\" || Array.isArray(target)) {\n\t\treturn `Alias \"${label}\" has a target that must be an object { harness, model, percent }`;\n\t}\n\tconst harness =\n\t\ttypeof target.harness === \"string\" ? target.harness.trim() : \"\";\n\tif (!harness) return `Alias \"${label}\" has a target without a harness`;\n\tif (harness === ALIAS_HARNESS_ID) {\n\t\treturn `Alias \"${label}\" cannot target the \"${ALIAS_HARNESS_ID}\" harness (aliases cannot point at aliases)`;\n\t}\n\tif (typeof target.model !== \"string\") {\n\t\treturn `Alias \"${label}\" has a target without a model`;\n\t}\n\tif (\n\t\ttypeof target.percent !== \"number\" ||\n\t\t!Number.isInteger(target.percent) ||\n\t\ttarget.percent < 1 ||\n\t\ttarget.percent > 100\n\t) {\n\t\treturn `Alias \"${label}\" has a target whose percent must be a whole number from 1 to 100`;\n\t}\n\treturn null;\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: validateAliasTargets\n * @description Validates a whole multi-target split: a non-empty array whose\n *   every target satisfies `validateAliasTarget` and whose percents sum to\n *   exactly 100 (users see percentages, never arbitrary weights).\n * @example validateAliasTargets([{ harness: \"pi\", model: \"m\", percent: 90 }, { harness: \"custom\", model: \"\", percent: 10 }], \"small\") => null\n * @param {unknown} targets - Candidate targets array.\n * @param {unknown} aliasName - Owning alias name (for error messages).\n * @returns {string|null} Error message, or null when valid.\n ***/\nexport function validateAliasTargets(targets, aliasName) {\n\tconst label =\n\t\tnormalizeAliasName(aliasName) || \"(unnamed alias)\";\n\tif (!Array.isArray(targets) || targets.length === 0) {\n\t\treturn `Alias \"${label}\" needs at least one target`;\n\t}\n\tfor (const target of targets) {\n\t\tconst reason = validateAliasTarget(target, aliasName);\n\t\tif (reason) return reason;\n\t}\n\tconst total = targets.reduce((sum, t) => sum + t.percent, 0);\n\tif (total !== 100) {\n\t\treturn `Alias \"${label}\" splits ${total}% — Percents must add up to 100%`;\n\t}\n\treturn null;\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: validateModelAlias\n * @description Validates one alias record, returning an error string or null.\n *   Two shapes are accepted: the legacy single-target record\n *   (`{ name, harness, model }`, read as one 100% target) and the weighted\n *   record (`{ name, targets: [{ harness, model, percent }] }` whose\n *   percents sum to 100). harness.trim() : \"\") ===\n\t\t\tALIAS_HARNESS_ID && Boolean(normalizeAliasName(model))\n\t);\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: getAliasTargets\n * @description Returns one alias record's weighted targets as fresh\n *   `{ harness, model, percent }` rows. Never throws — an absent\n *   or malformed record yields no targets.\n * @example getAliasTargets({ name: \"s\", harness: \"pi\", model: \"m\" }) => [{ harness: \"pi\", model: \"m\", percent: 100 }]\n * @param {unknown} alias - Alias record (either shape).\n * @returns {Array<{harness: string, model: string, percent: number}>} Target rows (possibly empty).\n ***/\nexport function getAliasTargets(alias) {\n\tif (!alias || typeof alias !== \"object\" || Array.isArray(alias)) return [];\n\tif (Array.isArray(alias.targets)) {\n\t\tconst out = [];\n\t\tfor (const target of alias.targets) {\n\t\t\tif (!target || typeof target !== \"object\" || Array.isArray(target)) {\n\t\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tconst harness =\n\t\t\t\ttypeof target.harness === \"string\" ? target.harness.trim() : \"\";\n\t\t\tconst model =\n\t\t\t\ttypeof target.model === \"string\" ? target.model.trim() : \"\";\n\t\t\tconst percent = target.percent;\n\t\t\tif (!harness || harness === ALIAS_HARNESS_ID) continue;\n\t\t\tif (\n\t\t\t\ttypeof percent !== \"number\" ||\n\t\t\t\t!Number.isInteger(percent) ||\n\t\t\t\tpercent < 1\n\t\t\t) {\n\t\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tout.push({ harness, model, percent });\n\t\t}\n\t\tif (out.length > 0) return out;\n\t}\n\tconst harness =\n\t\ttypeof alias.harness === \"string\" ? Powers the UI's one-click\n *   \"make the rows add to 100%\" helper; the API never auto-fixes splits\n *   (a non-100 payload is refused so the user sees the correction).\n * @example normalizeTargetPercents([{ harness: \"a\", model: \"m\" }, { harness: \"b\", model: \"n\" }]) => [{ harness: \"a\", model: \"m\", percent: 50 }, { harness: \"b\", model: \"n\", percent: 50 }]\n * @param {unknown} targets - Target rows (harness + model read, percent ignored).\n * @returns {Array<{harness: string, model: string, percent: number}>} Rows summing to exactly 100 (empty when input is empty).\n ***/\nexport function normalizeTargetPercents(targets) {\n\tconst rows = Array.isArray(targets)\n\t\t? targets\n\t\t\t\t.filter((t) => t && typeof t === \"object\" && !Array.isArray(t))\n\t\t\t\t.map((t) => ({\n\t\t\t\t\tharness: typeof t.harness === \"string\" ? t.harness.trim() : \"\",\n\t\t\t\t\tmodel: typeof t.model === \"string\" ? t.model : \"\",\n\t\t\t\t}))\n\t\t: [];\n\tif (rows.length === 0) return [];\n\tconst base = Math.floor(100 / rows.length);\n\tlet leftover = 100 - base * rows.length;\n\treturn rows.map((row) => {\n\t\tconst extra = leftover > 0 ? 1 : 0;\n\t\tleftover -= extra;\n\t\treturn { ...row, percent: base + extra };\n\t});\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: selectWeightedIndex\n * @description ONE deterministic step of smooth weighted round-robin: adds\n *   each weight to its running score, picks the highest scorer (lowest\n *   index wins ties), then subtracts the weight total from the winner so\n *   the next pick rotates. Never throws — garbage in stored JSON degrades to fewer\n *   aliases, not a broken project.\n * @example normalizeModelAliases([{ name: \" s \", harness: \"pi\", model: \"m\", extra: 1 }]) => [{ name: \"s\", harness: \"pi\", model: \"m\", targets: [{ harness: \"pi\", model: \"m\", percent: 100 }] }]\n * @param {unknown} list - Persisted `project.modelAliases` value.\n * @returns {Array<{name: string, harness: string, model: string, targets: Array}>} Clean alias records.\n ***/\nexport function normalizeModelAliases(list) {\n\tif (!Array.isArray(list)) return [];\n\tconst seen = new Set();\n\tconst out = [];\n\tfor (const entry of list) {\n\t\tif (validateModelAlias(entry)) continue;\n\t\tconst name = normalizeAliasName(entry.name);\n\t\tif (seen.has(name)) continue;\n\t\tseen.add(name);\n\t\tconst targets = getAliasTargets({\n\t\t\tharness:\n\t\t\t\ttypeof entry.harness === \"string\" ? {\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\tharness:\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\ttypeof t.harness === \"string\" ? t.harness.trim() : \"\",\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\tmodel: typeof t.model === \"string\" ? t.model : \"\",\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\tpercent: t.percent,\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t: t,\n\t\t\t\t\t)\n\t\t\t\t: undefined,\n\t\t});\n\t\tif (targets.length === 0) continue;\n\t\tout.push({\n\t\t\tname,\n\t\t\tharness: targets[0].harness,\n\t\t\tmodel: targets[0].model,\n\t\t\ttargets: targets.map((t) => ({ ...t })),\n\t\t});\n\t}\n\treturn out;\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: getAliasList\n * @description Returns the project's normalized alias list (never the live\n *   array — safe to map over even when the project never had aliases).\n * @example getAliasList({ modelAliases: [{ name: \"s\", harness: \"pi\", model: \"m\" }] }) => [{ name: \"s\", harness: \"pi\", model: \"m\" }]\n * @param {Object} [project] - Project entity.\n * @returns {Array<Object>} Normalized alias records (possibly empty).\n ***/\nexport function getAliasList(project) {\n\treturn normalizeModelAliases(project?.modelAliases);\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: resolveAlias\n * @description Looks up one alias by name on a project. Name matching is\n *   trimmed and case-sensitive (names are validated lowercase, so `Small`\n *   never silently resolves `small`).\n * @example resolveAlias(project, \"small\") => { name: \"small\", harness: \"pi\", model: \"google::m\" }\n * @param {Object} [project] - Project entity.\n * @param {unknown} name - Alias name.\n * @returns {Object|null} The alias record, or null when absent.\n ***/\nexport function resolveAlias(project, name) {\n\tconst wanted = normalizeAliasName(name);\n\tif (!wanted) return null;\n\treturn getAliasList(project).find((a) => a.name === wanted) || null;\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: findAliasUsages\n * @description Finds every stage (across all named workflows plus the legacy\n *   root stage list) and the project default that reference an alias name\n *   (`harness === \"alias\"` + `model === name`). Used by the settings UI to\n *   show impact (\"3 stages use this alias\") and to prove rename migration.\n * @example findAliasUsages(project, \"small\") => { stages: [{ workflowId, stageId, stageName }], usesAsDefault: true }\n * @param {Object} [project] - Project entity.\n * @param {unknown} name - Alias name.\n * @returns {{stages: Array<Object>, usesAsDefault: boolean}} Usage locations.\n ***/\nexport function findAliasUsages(project, name) {\n\tconst wanted = normalizeAliasName(name);\n\tconst usages = { stages: [], usesAsDefault: false };\n\tif (!wanted || !project || typeof project !== \"object\") return usages;\n\tif (\n\t\tisAliasRef(project.harness, project.defaultModel) &&\n\t\tnormalizeAliasName(project.defaultModel) === wanted\n\t) {\n\t\tusages.usesAsDefault = true;\n\t}\n\tconst checkStage = (workflowId, stage) => {\n\t\tif (!stage || typeof stage !== \"object\") return;\n\t\tif (\n\t\t\tisAliasRef(stage.harness, stage.model) &&\n\t\t\tnormalizeAliasName(stage.model) === wanted\n\t\t) {\n\t\t\tusages.stages.push({\n\t\t\t\tworkflowId: workflowId || null,\n\t\t\t\tstageId: stage.id ?? null,\n\t\t\t\tstageName: stage.name ?? null,\n\t\t\t});\n\t\t}\n\t};\n\tif (Array.isArray(project.workflows) && project.workflows.length > 0) {\n\t\t// Named workflows are authoritative (the legacy root list mirrors the\n\t\t// active workflow's stages as copies — scanning both double-counts).\n\t\tfor (const wf of project.workflows) {\n\t\t\tif (!wf || typeof wf !== \"object\") continue;\n\t\t\tfor (const stage of wf.stages || []) checkStage(wf.id, stage);\n\t\t}\n\t} else if (Array.isArray(project.stages)) {\n\t\tfor (const stage of project.stages) checkStage(null, stage);\n\t}\n\treturn usages;\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: applyAliasRename\n * @description Migrates every reference to an alias in place (project default\n *   + all workflow stages + legacy root stages) so a rename can never orphan\n *   stages. Mutates `project` and returns the number of references migrated.\n *   Both names are trimmed; a blank new name or identical names migrates\n *   nothing. Only exact alias references move — stages on other harnesses\n *   whose model merely equals the name are untouched.\n * @example applyAliasRename(project, \"small\", \"medium\") => 3\n * @param {Object} project - Project entity (mutated).\n * @param {unknown} oldName - Current alias name.\n * @param {unknown} newName - Replacement alias name.\n * @returns {number} Count of migrated references.\n ***/\nexport function applyAliasRename(project, oldName, newName) {\n\tconst from = normalizeAliasName(oldName);\n\tconst to = normalizeAliasName(newName);\n\tif (!project || typeof project !== \"object\" || !from || !to || from === to) {\n\t\treturn 0;\n\t}\n\tlet migrated = 0;\n\t// The project default stores its model in `defaultModel` (not `model`).\n\tif (\n\t\tisAliasRef(project.harness, project.defaultModel) &&\n\t\tnormalizeAliasName(project.defaultModel) === from\n\t) {\n\t\tproject.defaultModel = to;\n\t\tmigrated += 1;\n\t}\n\tconst migrateStages = (stages) => {\n\t\tif (!Array.isArray(stages)) return;\n\t\tfor (const stage of stages) {\n\t\t\tif (\n\t\t\t\tstage &&\n\t\t\t\ttypeof stage === \"object\" &&\n\t\t\t\tisAliasRef(stage.harness, stage.model) &&\n\t\t\t\tnormalizeAliasName(stage.model) === from\n\t\t\t) {\n\t\t\t\tstage.model = to;\n\t\t\t\tmigrated += 1;\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t};\n\tif (Array.isArray(project.workflows) && project.workflows.length > 0) {\n\t\t// Named workflows are authoritative (see findAliasUsages).\n\t\tfor (const wf of project.workflows) {\n\t\t\tif (wf && typeof wf === \"object\") migrateStages(wf.stages);\n\t\t}\n\t} else {\n\t\tmigrateStages(project.stages);\n\t}\n\treturn migrated;\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: aliasPseudoModels\n * @description Projects a project's aliases onto catalogue-shaped pseudo-models\n *   (`{ id, name, provider: \"alias\", key, harness: \"alias\" }`) for the virtual\n *   `alias` entry of the harness-first picker. Keys ARE the alias names, so\n *   the picker's exact-key matching, bare-name fallback, and provider\n *   grouping all work with zero picker forks.\n * @example aliasPseudoModels([{ name: \"small\", harness: \"pi\", model: \"m\" }]) => [{ id: \"small\", name: \"small\", provider: \"alias\", key: \"small\", harness: \"alias\" }]\n * @param {unknown} aliases - Alias records (any shape — normalized first).\n * @returns {Array<Object>} Pseudo-model rows (possibly empty).\n ***/\nexport function aliasPseudoModels(aliases) {\n\treturn normalizeModelAliases(aliases).map((a) => ({\n\t\tid: a.name,\n\t\tname: a.name,\n\t\tprovider: ALIAS_HARNESS_ID,\n\t\tkey: a.name,\n\t\tharness: ALIAS_HARNESS_ID,\n\t}));\n}\n","partials":"/***\n * MARK: modelAliases (shared alias grammar)\n * @description THE single implementation of the KainBain per-project model\n *   alias system, shared verbatim by the backend engine (`api/projectStore.js`,\n *   `api/agentRunner.js`, `api/sessionStore.js`) and the frontend settings UI\n *   (`frontend/src/components/settings/ModelAliasesSection.jsx`) so validation\n *   and resolution rules cannot drift. Plain ESM, zero dependencies.\n *\n *   An alias binds a short per-project name (e.g. `small`, `design`) to one\n *   or more weighted harness + model targets\n *   (`{ name, targets: [{ harness, model, percent }] }`, persisted on\n *   `project.modelAliases`; a legacy `{ name, harness, model }` record reads\n *   as one 100% target). Stages reference aliases through the\n *   existing harness-first fields — `harness: \"alias\"` + `model: \"<name>\"` —\n *   so every inherit/override path keeps working unchanged, and editing an\n *   alias changes every referencing stage with no stage edits (stages store\n *   the reference, never a copy of the concrete values).\n *\n *   `alias` is a VIRTUAL harness id: it never names a real AgentHarness\n *   (registering it throws — see `api/agent/harnessRegistry.js`), and an\n *   alias target pointing back at `alias` is a loop, treated as unknown.\n ***/\n\n/** The virtual harness id that scopes alias references. Never a real harness. */\nexport const ALIAS_HARNESS_ID = \"alias\";\n\n/** Alias names mirror the harness-id shape: lowercase, URL-safe. */\nexport const ALIAS_NAME_PATTERN = /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$/;\n\n/** Maximum alias name length (keeps picker labels and logs readable). */\nexport const ALIAS_NAME_MAX_LENGTH = 64;\n\n/***\n * MARK: normalizeAliasName\n * @description Trims an alias name to its usable form (\"\" when blank or\n *   non-string, i.e. \"no alias named\").\n * @example normalizeAliasName(\"  Small  \") => \"Small\"\n * @example normalizeAliasName(\"\") => \"\"\n * @param {unknown} name - Raw alias name.\n * @returns {string} Trimmed name, or \"\" when unset.\n ***/\nexport function normalizeAliasName(name) {\n\treturn typeof name === \"string\" ? name.trim() : \"\";\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: validateAliasName\n * @description Validates an alias name, returning an error string or null.\n *   Names are trimmed, 1–64 chars, and must match `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*`\n *   (case-sensitive: `Small` and `small` are different aliases, and uppercase\n *   is rejected so references cannot drift by case).\n * @example validateAliasName(\"small\") => null\n * @example validateAliasName(\"Small\") => \"…\"\n * @param {unknown} name - Raw alias name.\n * @returns {string|null} Error message, or null when valid.\n ***/\nexport function validateAliasName(name) {\n\tconst trimmed = normalizeAliasName(name);\n\tif (!trimmed) return \"Alias name is required\";\n\tif (trimmed.length > ALIAS_NAME_MAX_LENGTH) {\n\t\treturn `Alias name must be at most ${ALIAS_NAME_MAX_LENGTH} characters`;\n\t}\n\tif (!ALIAS_NAME_PATTERN.test(trimmed)) {\n\t\treturn \"Alias name must start with a letter or digit and contain only lowercase letters, digits, - and _\";\n\t}\n\treturn null;\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: validateAliasTarget\n * @description Validates ONE weighted target inside a multi-target alias,\n *   returning an error string or null. The target harness must be a\n *   non-empty string that is NOT the virtual `alias` id (loop guard). The\n *   target model is a string in any accepted model-key form (blank is\n *   allowed at the grammar level for self-managed `none` harnesses — the\n *   settings UI additionally requires a model for `list` harnesses). The\n *   percent is an integer 1–100 (the rows of one alias must sum to exactly\n *   100 — see `validateAliasTargets`).\n * @example validateAliasTarget({ harness: \"pi\", model: \"google::m\", percent: 90 }, \"small\") => null\n * @example validateAliasTarget({ harness: \"pi\", model: \"m\", percent: 0 }, \"small\") => \"…\"\n * @param {unknown} target - Candidate `{ harness, model, percent }` record.\n * @param {unknown} aliasName - Owning alias name (for error messages).\n * @returns {string|null} Error message, or null when valid.\n ***/\nexport function validateAliasTarget(target, aliasName) {\n\tconst label =\n\t\tnormalizeAliasName(aliasName) || \"(unnamed alias)\";\n\tif (!target || typeof target !== \"object\" || Array.isArray(target)) {\n\t\treturn `Alias \"${label}\" has a target that must be an object { harness, model, percent }`;\n\t}\n\tconst harness =\n\t\ttypeof target.harness === \"string\" ? target.harness.trim() : \"\";\n\tif (!harness) return `Alias \"${label}\" has a target without a harness`;\n\tif (harness === ALIAS_HARNESS_ID) {\n\t\treturn `Alias \"${label}\" cannot target the \"${ALIAS_HARNESS_ID}\" harness (aliases cannot point at aliases)`;\n\t}\n\tif (typeof target.model !== \"string\") {\n\t\treturn `Alias \"${label}\" has a target without a model`;\n\t}\n\tif (\n\t\ttypeof target.percent !== \"number\" ||\n\t\t!Number.isInteger(target.percent) ||\n\t\ttarget.percent < 1 ||\n\t\ttarget.percent > 100\n\t) {\n\t\treturn `Alias \"${label}\" has a target whose percent must be a whole number from 1 to 100`;\n\t}\n\treturn null;\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: validateAliasTargets\n * @description Validates a whole multi-target split: a non-empty array whose\n *   every target satisfies `validateAliasTarget` and whose percents sum to\n *   exactly 100 (users see percentages, never arbitrary weights).\n * @example validateAliasTargets([{ harness: \"pi\", model: \"m\", percent: 90 }, { harness: \"custom\", model: \"\", percent: 10 }], \"small\") => null\n * @param {unknown} targets - Candidate targets array.\n * @param {unknown} aliasName - Owning alias name (for error messages).\n * @returns {string|null} Error message, or null when valid.\n ***/\nexport function validateAliasTargets(targets, aliasName) {\n\tconst label =\n\t\tnormalizeAliasName(aliasName) || \"(unnamed alias)\";\n\tif (!Array.isArray(targets) || targets.length === 0) {\n\t\treturn `Alias \"${label}\" needs at least one target`;\n\t}\n\tfor (const target of targets) {\n\t\tconst reason = validateAliasTarget(target, aliasName);\n\t\tif (reason) return reason;\n\t}\n\tconst total = targets.reduce((sum, t) => sum + t.percent, 0);\n\tif (total !== 100) {\n\t\treturn `Alias \"${label}\" splits ${total}% — Percents must add up to 100%`;\n\t}\n\treturn null;\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: validateModelAlias\n * @description Validates one alias record, returning an error string or null.\n *   Two shapes are accepted: the legacy single-target record\n *   (`{ name, harness, model }`, read as one 100% target) and the weighted\n *   record (`{ name, targets: [{ harness, model, percent }] }` whose\n *   percents sum to 100). A lone target harness must be a non-empty string\n *   that is NOT the virtual `alias` id (loop guard); the model accepts any\n *   model-key form, EXCEPT blank is allowed only for self-managed harnesses\n *   at dispatch (the settings UI requires a model for `list` harnesses).\n * @example validateModelAlias({ name: \"small\", harness: \"pi\", model: \"google::m\" }) => null\n * @example validateModelAlias({ name: \"c\", harness: \"custom\", model: \"\" }) => null\n * @param {unknown} entry - Candidate alias record.\n * @returns {string|null} Error message, or null when valid.\n ***/\nexport function validateModelAlias(entry) {\n\tif (!entry || typeof entry !== \"object\" || Array.isArray(entry)) {\n\t\treturn \"Alias must be an object { name, targets }\";\n\t}\n\tconst nameError = validateAliasName(entry.name);\n\tif (nameError) return nameError;\n\tif (entry.targets !== undefined && entry.targets !== null) {\n\t\treturn validateAliasTargets(entry.targets, entry.name);\n\t}\n\tconst harness =\n\t\ttypeof entry.harness === \"string\" ? entry.harness.trim() : \"\";\n\tif (!harness) return `Alias \"${normalizeAliasName(entry.name)}\" needs a harness`;\n\tif (harness === ALIAS_HARNESS_ID) {\n\t\treturn `Alias \"${normalizeAliasName(entry.name)}\" cannot target the \"${ALIAS_HARNESS_ID}\" harness (aliases cannot point at aliases)`;\n\t}\n\tif (typeof entry.model !== \"string\") {\n\t\treturn `Alias \"${normalizeAliasName(entry.name)}\" needs a model`;\n\t}\n\treturn null;\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: isAliasRef\n * @description Whether a harness + model pair is an alias reference\n *   (`harness === \"alias\"` with a non-blank model naming the alias).\n * @example isAliasRef(\"alias\", \"small\") => true\n * @example isAliasRef(\"pi\", \"small\") => false\n * @param {unknown} harness - Effective harness id.\n * @param {unknown} model - Effective model value (the alias name).\n * @returns {boolean} True when the pair references an alias.\n ***/\nexport function isAliasRef(harness, model) {\n\treturn (\n\t\t(typeof harness === \"string\" ? harness.trim() : \"\") ===\n\t\t\tALIAS_HARNESS_ID && Boolean(normalizeAliasName(model))\n\t);\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: getAliasTargets\n * @description Returns one alias record's weighted targets as fresh\n *   `{ harness, model, percent }` rows. A legacy single-target record\n *   (`{ harness, model }` with no `targets`) reads as one 100% target, so\n *   every consumer downstream sees a single shape. Never throws — an absent\n *   or malformed record yields no targets.\n * @example getAliasTargets({ name: \"s\", harness: \"pi\", model: \"m\" }) => [{ harness: \"pi\", model: \"m\", percent: 100 }]\n * @param {unknown} alias - Alias record (either shape).\n * @returns {Array<{harness: string, model: string, percent: number}>} Target rows (possibly empty).\n ***/\nexport function getAliasTargets(alias) {\n\tif (!alias || typeof alias !== \"object\" || Array.isArray(alias)) return [];\n\tif (Array.isArray(alias.targets)) {\n\t\tconst out = [];\n\t\tfor (const target of alias.targets) {\n\t\t\tif (!target || typeof target !== \"object\" || Array.isArray(target)) {\n\t\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tconst harness =\n\t\t\t\ttypeof target.harness === \"string\" ? target.harness.trim() : \"\";\n\t\t\tconst model =\n\t\t\t\ttypeof target.model === \"string\" ? target.model.trim() : \"\";\n\t\t\tconst percent = target.percent;\n\t\t\tif (!harness || harness === ALIAS_HARNESS_ID) continue;\n\t\t\tif (\n\t\t\t\ttypeof percent !== \"number\" ||\n\t\t\t\t!Number.isInteger(percent) ||\n\t\t\t\tpercent < 1\n\t\t\t) {\n\t\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tout.push({ harness, model, percent });\n\t\t}\n\t\tif (out.length > 0) return out;\n\t}\n\tconst harness =\n\t\ttypeof alias.harness === \"string\" ? alias.harness.trim() : \"\";\n\tif (!harness || harness === ALIAS_HARNESS_ID) return [];\n\tif (typeof alias.model !== \"string\") return [];\n\treturn [{ harness, model: alias.model.trim(), percent: 100 }];\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: aliasTargetsSignature\n * @description Builds the canonical fingerprint of an alias's targets\n *   (trimmed harness + model with percent, joined) so rename inference,\n *   selector counters, and tests can tell \"same split\" from \"retargeted\"\n *   without caring about the legacy/new record shape.\n * @example aliasTargetsSignature({ name: \"s\", harness: \"pi\", model: \"m\" }) => \"pi::m@100\"\n * @param {unknown} alias - Alias record (either shape).\n * @returns {string} Canonical signature (\"\" when the alias has no targets).\n ***/\nexport function aliasTargetsSignature(alias) {\n\treturn getAliasTargets(alias)\n\t\t.map((t) => `${t.harness}::${t.model}@${t.percent}`)\n\t\t.join(\"|\");\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: normalizeTargetPercents\n * @description Spreads 100% evenly across the given targets (largest share\n *   first for the leftover points, so thirds become 34/33/33), returning\n *   fresh rows with the same harness + model. Powers the UI's one-click\n *   \"make the rows add to 100%\" helper; the API never auto-fixes splits\n *   (a non-100 payload is refused so the user sees the correction).\n * @example normalizeTargetPercents([{ harness: \"a\", model: \"m\" }, { harness: \"b\", model: \"n\" }]) => [{ harness: \"a\", model: \"m\", percent: 50 }, { harness: \"b\", model: \"n\", percent: 50 }]\n * @param {unknown} targets - Target rows (harness + model read, percent ignored).\n * @returns {Array<{harness: string, model: string, percent: number}>} Rows summing to exactly 100 (empty when input is empty).\n ***/\nexport function normalizeTargetPercents(targets) {\n\tconst rows = Array.isArray(targets)\n\t\t? targets\n\t\t\t\t.filter((t) => t && typeof t === \"object\" && !Array.isArray(t))\n\t\t\t\t.map((t) => ({\n\t\t\t\t\tharness: typeof t.harness === \"string\" ? t.harness.trim() : \"\",\n\t\t\t\t\tmodel: typeof t.model === \"string\" ? t.model : \"\",\n\t\t\t\t}))\n\t\t: [];\n\tif (rows.length === 0) return [];\n\tconst base = Math.floor(100 / rows.length);\n\tlet leftover = 100 - base * rows.length;\n\treturn rows.map((row) => {\n\t\tconst extra = leftover > 0 ? 1 : 0;\n\t\tleftover -= extra;\n\t\treturn { ...row, percent: base + extra };\n\t});\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: selectWeightedIndex\n * @description ONE deterministic step of smooth weighted round-robin: adds\n *   each weight to its running score, picks the highest scorer (lowest\n *   index wins ties), then subtracts the weight total from the winner so\n *   the next pick rotates. With weights [90, 10] the minority index wins\n *   exactly every 10th call, evenly spread — no random clustering, and the\n *   sequence replays exactly from a zeroed score array (scores are kept\n *   outside so the caller owns persistence: in-memory counters in\n *   `api/aliasSelector.js`, injectable arrays in tests).\n * @example selectWeightedIndex([90, 10], [0, 0]) => 0\n * @param {Array<number>} weights - Per-target weights (the integer percents).\n * @param {Array<number>} scores - Running scores, mutated in place (must match weights in length).\n * @returns {number} Winning index (-1 when there is nothing to pick).\n ***/\nexport function selectWeightedIndex(weights, scores) {\n\tif (!Array.isArray(weights) || weights.length === 0) return -1;\n\tconst total = weights.reduce(\n\t\t(sum, w) => sum + (typeof w === \"number\" && w > 0 ? w : 0),\n\t\t0,\n\t);\n\tif (total <= 0) return -1;\n\tlet winner = 0;\n\tlet best = -Infinity;\n\tfor (let i = 0; i < weights.length; i++) {\n\t\tconst weight = typeof weights[i] === \"number\" && weights[i] > 0 ? weights[i] : 0;\n\t\tscores[i] = (typeof scores[i] === \"number\" ? scores[i] : 0) + weight;\n\t\tif (scores[i] > best) {\n\t\t\tbest = scores[i];\n\t\t\twinner = i;\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tscores[winner] -= total;\n\treturn winner;\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: normalizeModelAliases\n * @description Normalizes a persisted alias list on write: drops non-objects\n *   and invalid entries, trims every field, upgrades legacy single-target\n *   records to the weighted form, dedupes by name (first wins), and returns\n *   fresh canonical records. Every record carries `targets`\n *   (`[{ harness, model, percent }]`, percents summing to 100) with the\n *   first target mirrored onto the legacy `harness`/`model` fields, so a\n *   rollback build that only reads the legacy fields keeps serving the top\n *   target. Never throws — garbage in stored JSON degrades to fewer\n *   aliases, not a broken project.\n * @example normalizeModelAliases([{ name: \" s \", harness: \"pi\", model: \"m\", extra: 1 }]) => [{ name: \"s\", harness: \"pi\", model: \"m\", targets: [{ harness: \"pi\", model: \"m\", percent: 100 }] }]\n * @param {unknown} list - Persisted `project.modelAliases` value.\n * @returns {Array<{name: string, harness: string, model: string, targets: Array}>} Clean alias records.\n ***/\nexport function normalizeModelAliases(list) {\n\tif (!Array.isArray(list)) return [];\n\tconst seen = new Set();\n\tconst out = [];\n\tfor (const entry of list) {\n\t\tif (validateModelAlias(entry)) continue;\n\t\tconst name = normalizeAliasName(entry.name);\n\t\tif (seen.has(name)) continue;\n\t\tseen.add(name);\n\t\tconst targets = getAliasTargets({\n\t\t\tharness:\n\t\t\t\ttypeof entry.harness === \"string\" ? entry.harness.trim() : \"\",\n\t\t\tmodel: typeof entry.model === \"string\" ? entry.model : \"\",\n\t\t\ttargets: Array.isArray(entry.targets)\n\t\t\t\t? entry.targets.map((t) =>\n\t\t\t\t\t\tt && typeof t === \"object\" && !Array.isArray(t)\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t? {\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\tharness:\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\ttypeof t.harness === \"string\" ? t.harness.trim() : \"\",\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\tmodel: typeof t.model === \"string\" ? t.model : \"\",\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\tpercent: t.percent,\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t: t,\n\t\t\t\t\t)\n\t\t\t\t: undefined,\n\t\t});\n\t\tif (targets.length === 0) continue;\n\t\tout.push({\n\t\t\tname,\n\t\t\tharness: targets[0].harness,\n\t\t\tmodel: targets[0].model,\n\t\t\ttargets: targets.map((t) => ({ ...t })),\n\t\t});\n\t}\n\treturn out;\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: getAliasList\n * @description Returns the project's normalized alias list (never the live\n *   array — safe to map over even when the project never had aliases).\n * @example getAliasList({ modelAliases: [{ name: \"s\", harness: \"pi\", model: \"m\" }] }) => [{ name: \"s\", harness: \"pi\", model: \"m\" }]\n * @param {Object} [project] - Project entity.\n * @returns {Array<Object>} Normalized alias records (possibly empty).\n ***/\nexport function getAliasList(project) {\n\treturn normalizeModelAliases(project?.modelAliases);\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: resolveAlias\n * @description Looks up one alias by name on a project. Used by the settings UI to\n *   show impact (\"3 stages use this alias\") and to prove rename migration.\n * @example findAliasUsages(project, \"small\") => { stages: [{ workflowId, stageId, stageName }], usesAsDefault: true }\n * @param {Object} [project] - Project entity.\n * @param {unknown} name - Alias name.\n * @returns {{stages: Array<Object>, usesAsDefault: boolean}} Usage locations.\n ***/\nexport function findAliasUsages(project, name) {\n\tconst wanted = normalizeAliasName(name);\n\tconst usages = { stages: [], usesAsDefault: false };\n\tif (!wanted || !project || typeof project !== \"object\") return usages;\n\tif (\n\t\tisAliasRef(project.harness, project.defaultModel) &&\n\t\tnormalizeAliasName(project.defaultModel) === wanted\n\t) {\n\t\tusages.usesAsDefault = true;\n\t}\n\tconst checkStage = (workflowId, stage) => {\n\t\tif (!stage || typeof stage !== \"object\") return;\n\t\tif (\n\t\t\tisAliasRef(stage.harness, stage.model) &&\n\t\t\tnormalizeAliasName(stage.model) === wanted\n\t\t) {\n\t\t\tusages.stages.push({\n\t\t\t\tworkflowId: workflowId || null,\n\t\t\t\tstageId: stage.id ?? null,\n\t\t\t\tstageName: stage.name ?? null,\n\t\t\t});\n\t\t}\n\t};\n\tif (Array.isArray(project.workflows) && project.workflows.length > 0) {\n\t\t// Named workflows are authoritative (the legacy root list mirrors the\n\t\t// active workflow's stages as copies — scanning both double-counts).\n\t\tfor (const wf of project.workflows) {\n\t\t\tif (!wf || typeof wf !== \"object\") continue;\n\t\t\tfor (const stage of wf.stages || []) checkStage(wf.id, stage);\n\t\t}\n\t} else if (Array.isArray(project.stages)) {\n\t\tfor (const stage of project.stages) checkStage(null, stage);\n\t}\n\treturn usages;\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: applyAliasRename\n * @description Migrates every reference to an alias in place (project default\n *   + all workflow stages + legacy root stages) so a rename can never orphan\n *   stages. Mutates `project` and returns the number of references migrated.\n *   Both names are trimmed; a blank new name or identical names migrates\n *   nothing. Only exact alias references move — stages on other harnesses\n *   whose model merely equals the name are untouched.\n * @example applyAliasRename(project, \"small\", \"medium\") => 3\n * @param {Object} project - Project entity (mutated).\n * @param {unknown} oldName - Current alias name.\n * @param {unknown} newName - Replacement alias name.\n * @returns {number} Count of migrated references.\n ***/\nexport function applyAliasRename(project, oldName, newName) {\n\tconst from = normalizeAliasName(oldName);\n\tconst to = normalizeAliasName(newName);\n\tif (!project || typeof project !== \"object\" || !from || !to || from === to) {\n\t\treturn 0;\n\t}\n\tlet migrated = 0;\n\t// The project default stores its model in `defaultModel` (not `model`).\n\tif (\n\t\tisAliasRef(project.harness, project.defaultModel) &&\n\t\tnormalizeAliasName(project.defaultModel) === from\n\t) {\n\t\tproject.defaultModel = to;\n\t\tmigrated += 1;\n\t}\n\tconst migrateStages = (stages) => {\n\t\tif (!Array.isArray(stages)) return;\n\t\tfor (const stage of stages) {\n\t\t\tif (\n\t\t\t\tstage &&\n\t\t\t\ttypeof stage === \"object\" &&\n\t\t\t\tisAliasRef(stage.harness, stage.model) &&\n\t\t\t\tnormalizeAliasName(stage.model) === from\n\t\t\t) {\n\t\t\t\tstage.model = to;\n\t\t\t\tmigrated += 1;\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t};\n\tif (Array.isArray(project.workflows) && project.workflows.length > 0) {\n\t\t// Named workflows are authoritative (see findAliasUsages).\n\t\tfor (const wf of project.workflows) {\n\t\t\tif (wf && typeof wf === \"object\") migrateStages(wf.stages);\n\t\t}\n\t} else {\n\t\tmigrateStages(project.stages);\n\t}\n\treturn migrated;\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: aliasPseudoModels\n * @description Projects a project's aliases onto catalogue-shaped pseudo-models\n *   (`{ id, name, provider: \"alias\", key, harness: \"alias\" }`) for the virtual\n *   `alias` entry of the harness-first picker. Plain ESM, zero dependencies.\n *\n *   An alias binds a short per-project name (e.g. `small`, `design`) to one\n *   or more weighted harness + model targets\n *   (`{ name, targets: [{ harness, model, percent }] }`, persisted on\n *   `project.modelAliases`; a legacy `{ name, harness, model }` record reads\n *   as one 100% target). Stages reference aliases through the\n *   existing harness-first fields — `harness: \"alias\"` + `model: \"<name>\"` —\n *   so every inherit/override path keeps working unchanged, and editing an\n *   alias changes every referencing stage with no stage edits (stages store\n *   the reference, never a copy of the concrete values).\n *\n *   `alias` is a VIRTUAL harness id: it never names a real AgentHarness\n *   (registering it throws — see `api/agent/harnessRegistry.js`), and an\n *   alias target pointing back at `alias` is a loop, treated as unknown.\n ***/\n\n/** The virtual harness id that scopes alias references. Never a real harness. */\nexport const ALIAS_HARNESS_ID = \"alias\";\n\n/** Alias names mirror the harness-id shape: lowercase, URL-safe. */\nexport const ALIAS_NAME_PATTERN = /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$/;\n\n/** Maximum alias name length (keeps picker labels and logs readable). */\nexport const ALIAS_NAME_MAX_LENGTH = 64;\n\n/***\n * MARK: normalizeAliasName\n * @description Trims an alias name to its usable form (\"\" when blank or\n *   non-string, i.e. \"no alias named\").\n * @example normalizeAliasName(\"  Small  \") => \"Small\"\n * @example normalizeAliasName(\"\") => \"\"\n * @param {unknown} name - Raw alias name.\n * @returns {string} Trimmed name, or \"\" when unset.\n ***/\nexport function normalizeAliasName(name) {\n\treturn typeof name === \"string\" ? name.trim() : \"\";\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: validateAliasName\n * @description Validates an alias name, returning an error string or null.\n *   Names are trimmed, 1–64 chars, and must match `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*`\n *   (case-sensitive: `Small` and `small` are different aliases, and uppercase\n *   is rejected so references cannot drift by case).\n * @example validateAliasName(\"small\") => null\n * @example validateAliasName(\"Small\") => \"…\"\n * @param {unknown} name - Raw alias name.\n * @returns {string|null} Error message, or null when valid.\n ***/\nexport function validateAliasName(name) {\n\tconst trimmed = normalizeAliasName(name);\n\tif (!trimmed) return \"Alias name is required\";\n\tif (trimmed.length > ALIAS_NAME_MAX_LENGTH) {\n\t\treturn `Alias name must be at most ${ALIAS_NAME_MAX_LENGTH} characters`;\n\t}\n\tif (!ALIAS_NAME_PATTERN.test(trimmed)) {\n\t\treturn \"Alias name must start with a letter or digit and contain only lowercase letters, digits, - and _\";\n\t}\n\treturn null;\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: validateAliasTarget\n * @description Validates ONE weighted target inside a multi-target alias,\n *   returning an error string or null. The target harness must be a\n *   non-empty string that is NOT the virtual `alias` id (loop guard). The\n *   target model is a string in any accepted model-key form (blank is\n *   allowed at the grammar level for self-managed `none` harnesses — the\n *   settings UI additionally requires a model for `list` harnesses). The\n *   percent is an integer 1–100 (the rows of one alias must sum to exactly\n *   100 — see `validateAliasTargets`).\n * @example validateAliasTarget({ harness: \"pi\", model: \"google::m\", percent: 90 }, \"small\") => null\n * @example validateAliasTarget({ harness: \"pi\", model: \"m\", percent: 0 }, \"small\") => \"…\"\n * @param {unknown} target - Candidate `{ harness, model, percent }` record.\n * @param {unknown} aliasName - Owning alias name (for error messages).\n * @returns {string|null} Error message, or null when valid.\n ***/\nexport function validateAliasTarget(target, aliasName) {\n\tconst label =\n\t\tnormalizeAliasName(aliasName) || \"(unnamed alias)\";\n\tif (!target || typeof target !== \"object\" || Array.isArray(target)) {\n\t\treturn `Alias \"${label}\" has a target that must be an object { harness, model, percent }`;\n\t}\n\tconst harness =\n\t\ttypeof target.harness === \"string\" ? target.harness.trim() : \"\";\n\tif (!harness) return `Alias \"${label}\" has a target without a harness`;\n\tif (harness === ALIAS_HARNESS_ID) {\n\t\treturn `Alias \"${label}\" cannot target the \"${ALIAS_HARNESS_ID}\" harness (aliases cannot point at aliases)`;\n\t}\n\tif (typeof target.model !== \"string\") {\n\t\treturn `Alias \"${label}\" has a target without a model`;\n\t}\n\tif (\n\t\ttypeof target.percent !== \"number\" ||\n\t\t!Number.isInteger(target.percent) ||\n\t\ttarget.percent < 1 ||\n\t\ttarget.percent > 100\n\t) {\n\t\treturn `Alias \"${label}\" has a target whose percent must be a whole number from 1 to 100`;\n\t}\n\treturn null;\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: validateAliasTargets\n * @description Validates a whole multi-target split: a non-empty array whose\n *   every target satisfies `validateAliasTarget` and whose percents sum to\n *   exactly 100 (users see percentages, never arbitrary weights).\n * @example validateAliasTargets([{ harness: \"pi\", model: \"m\", percent: 90 }, { harness: \"custom\", model: \"\", percent: 10 }], \"small\") => null\n * @param {unknown} targets - Candidate targets array.\n * @param {unknown} aliasName - Owning alias name (for error messages).\n * @returns {string|null} Error message, or null when valid.\n ***/\nexport function validateAliasTargets(targets, aliasName) {\n\tconst label =\n\t\tnormalizeAliasName(aliasName) || \"(unnamed alias)\";\n\tif (!Array.isArray(targets) || targets.length === 0) {\n\t\treturn `Alias \"${label}\" needs at least one target`;\n\t}\n\tfor (const target of targets) {\n\t\tconst reason = validateAliasTarget(target, aliasName);\n\t\tif (reason) return reason;\n\t}\n\tconst total = targets.reduce((sum, t) => sum + t.percent, 0);\n\tif (total !== 100) {\n\t\treturn `Alias \"${label}\" splits ${total}% — Percents must add up to 100%`;\n\t}\n\treturn null;\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: validateModelAlias\n * @description Validates one alias record, returning an error string or null.\n *   Two shapes are accepted: the legacy single-target record\n *   (`{ name, harness, model }`, read as one 100% target) and the weighted\n *   record (`{ name, targets: [{ harness, model, percent }] }` whose\n *   percents sum to 100). A lone target harness must be a non-empty string\n *   that is NOT the virtual `alias` id (loop guard); the model accepts any\n *   model-key form, EXCEPT blank is allowed only for self-managed harnesses\n *   at dispatch (the settings UI requires a model for `list` harnesses).\n * @example validateModelAlias({ name: \"small\", harness: \"pi\", model: \"google::m\" }) => null\n * @example validateModelAlias({ name: \"c\", harness: \"custom\", model: \"\" }) => null\n * @param {unknown} entry - Candidate alias record.\n * @returns {string|null} Error message, or null when valid.\n ***/\nexport function validateModelAlias(entry) {\n\tif (!entry || typeof entry !== \"object\" || Array.isArray(entry)) {\n\t\treturn \"Alias must be an object { name, targets }\";\n\t}\n\tconst nameError = validateAliasName(entry.name);\n\tif (nameError) return nameError;\n\tif (entry.targets !== undefined && entry.targets !== null) {\n\t\treturn validateAliasTargets(entry.targets, entry.name);\n\t}\n\tconst harness =\n\t\ttypeof entry.harness === \"string\" ? entry.harness.trim() : \"\";\n\tif (!harness) return `Alias \"${normalizeAliasName(entry.name)}\" needs a harness`;\n\tif (harness === ALIAS_HARNESS_ID) {\n\t\treturn `Alias \"${normalizeAliasName(entry.name)}\" cannot target the \"${ALIAS_HARNESS_ID}\" harness (aliases cannot point at aliases)`;\n\t}\n\tif (typeof entry.model !== \"string\") {\n\t\treturn `Alias \"${normalizeAliasName(entry.name)}\" needs a model`;\n\t}\n\treturn null;\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: isAliasRef\n * @description Whether a harness + model pair is an alias reference\n *   (`harness === \"alias\"` with a non-blank model naming the alias).\n * @example isAliasRef(\"alias\", \"small\") => true\n * @example isAliasRef(\"pi\", \"small\") => false\n * @param {unknown} harness - Effective harness id.\n * @param {unknown} model - Effective model value (the alias name).\n * @returns {boolean} True when the pair references an alias.\n ***/\nexport function isAliasRef(harness, model) {\n\treturn (\n\t\t(typeof harness === \"string\" ? harness.trim() : \"\") ===\n\t\t\tALIAS_HARNESS_ID && Boolean(normalizeAliasName(model))\n\t);\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: getAliasTargets\n * @description Returns one alias record's weighted targets as fresh\n *   `{ harness, model, percent }` rows. Never throws — an absent\n *   or malformed record yields no targets.\n * @example getAliasTargets({ name: \"s\", harness: \"pi\", model: \"m\" }) => [{ harness: \"pi\", model: \"m\", percent: 100 }]\n * @param {unknown} alias - Alias record (either shape).\n * @returns {Array<{harness: string, model: string, percent: number}>} Target rows (possibly empty).\n ***/\nexport function getAliasTargets(alias) {\n\tif (!alias || typeof alias !== \"object\" || Array.isArray(alias)) return [];\n\tif (Array.isArray(alias.targets)) {\n\t\tconst out = [];\n\t\tfor (const target of alias.targets) {\n\t\t\tif (!target || typeof target !== \"object\" || Array.isArray(target)) {\n\t\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tconst harness =\n\t\t\t\ttypeof target.harness === \"string\" ? target.harness.trim() : \"\";\n\t\t\tconst model =\n\t\t\t\ttypeof target.model === \"string\" ? target.model.trim() : \"\";\n\t\t\tconst percent = target.percent;\n\t\t\tif (!harness || harness === ALIAS_HARNESS_ID) continue;\n\t\t\tif (\n\t\t\t\ttypeof percent !== \"number\" ||\n\t\t\t\t!Number.isInteger(percent) ||\n\t\t\t\tpercent < 1\n\t\t\t) {\n\t\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tout.push({ harness, model, percent });\n\t\t}\n\t\tif (out.length > 0) return out;\n\t}\n\tconst harness =\n\t\ttypeof alias.harness === \"string\" ? alias.harness.trim() : \"\";\n\tif (!harness || harness === ALIAS_HARNESS_ID) return [];\n\tif (typeof alias.model !== \"string\") return [];\n\treturn [{ harness, model: alias.model.trim(), percent: 100 }];\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: aliasTargetsSignature\n * @description Builds the canonical fingerprint of an alias's targets\n *   (trimmed harness + model with percent, joined) so rename inference,\n *   selector counters, and tests can tell \"same split\" from \"retargeted\"\n *   without caring about the legacy/new record shape.\n * @example aliasTargetsSignature({ name: \"s\", harness: \"pi\", model: \"m\" }) => \"pi::m@100\"\n * @param {unknown} alias - Alias record (either shape).\n * @returns {string} Canonical signature (\"\" when the alias has no targets).\n ***/\nexport function aliasTargetsSignature(alias) {\n\treturn getAliasTargets(alias)\n\t\t.map((t) => `${t.harness}::${t.model}@${t.percent}`)\n\t\t.join(\"|\");\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: normalizeTargetPercents\n * @description Spreads 100% evenly across the given targets (largest share\n *   first for the leftover points, so thirds become 34/33/33), returning\n *   fresh rows with the same harness + model. Powers the UI's one-click\n *   \"make the rows add to 100%\" helper; the API never auto-fixes splits\n *   (a non-100 payload is refused so the user sees the correction).\n * @example normalizeTargetPercents([{ harness: \"a\", model: \"m\" }, { harness: \"b\", model: \"n\" }]) => [{ harness: \"a\", model: \"m\", percent: 50 }, { harness: \"b\", model: \"n\", percent: 50 }]\n * @param {unknown} targets - Target rows (harness + model read, percent ignored).\n * @returns {Array<{harness: string, model: string, percent: number}>} Rows summing to exactly 100 (empty when input is empty).\n ***/\nexport function normalizeTargetPercents(targets) {\n\tconst rows = Array.isArray(targets)\n\t\t? targets\n\t\t\t\t.filter((t) => t && typeof t === \"object\" && !Array.isArray(t))\n\t\t\t\t.map((t) => ({\n\t\t\t\t\tharness: typeof t.harness === \"string\" ? t.harness.trim() : \"\",\n\t\t\t\t\tmodel: typeof t.model === \"string\" ? t.model : \"\",\n\t\t\t\t}))\n\t\t: [];\n\tif (rows.length === 0) return [];\n\tconst base = Math.floor(100 / rows.length);\n\tlet leftover = 100 - base * rows.length;\n\treturn rows.map((row) => {\n\t\tconst extra = leftover > 0 ? 1 : 0;\n\t\tleftover -= extra;\n\t\treturn { ...row, percent: base + extra };\n\t});\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: selectWeightedIndex\n * @description ONE deterministic step of smooth weighted round-robin: adds\n *   each weight to its running score, picks the highest scorer (lowest\n *   index wins ties), then subtracts the weight total from the winner so\n *   the next pick rotates. With weights [90, 10] the minority index wins\n *   exactly every 10th call, evenly spread — no random clustering, and the\n *   sequence replays exactly from a zeroed score array (scores are kept\n *   outside so the caller owns persistence: in-memory counters in\n *   `api/aliasSelector.js`, injectable arrays in tests).\n * @example selectWeightedIndex([90, 10], [0, 0]) => 0\n * @param {Array<number>} weights - Per-target weights (the integer percents).\n * @param {Array<number>} scores - Running scores, mutated in place (must match weights in length).\n * @returns {number} Winning index (-1 when there is nothing to pick).\n ***/\nexport function selectWeightedIndex(weights, scores) {\n\tif (!Array.isArray(weights) || weights.length === 0) return -1;\n\tconst total = weights.reduce(\n\t\t(sum, w) => sum + (typeof w === \"number\" && w > 0 ? w : 0),\n\t\t0,\n\t);\n\tif (total <= 0) return -1;\n\tlet winner = 0;\n\tlet best = -Infinity;\n\tfor (let i = 0; i < weights.length; i++) {\n\t\tconst weight = typeof weights[i] === \"number\" && weights[i] > 0 ? weights[i] : 0;\n\t\tscores[i] = (typeof scores[i] === \"number\" ? scores[i] : 0) + weight;\n\t\tif (scores[i] > best) {\n\t\t\tbest = scores[i];\n\t\t\twinner = i;\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tscores[winner] -= total;\n\treturn winner;\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: normalizeModelAliases\n * @description Normalizes a persisted alias list on write: drops non-objects\n *   and invalid entries, trims every field, upgrades legacy single-target\n *   records to the weighted form, dedupes by name (first wins), and returns\n *   fresh canonical records. Every record carries `targets`\n *   (`[{ harness, model, percent }]`, percents summing to 100) with the\n *   first target mirrored onto the legacy `harness`/`model` fields, so a\n *   rollback build that only reads the legacy fields keeps serving the top\n *   target.
