So the goal of code should make it the most understandable with zero context as possible\n\n### Principles\n\n- Long variables names where needed to be descriptive\n- Avoid using technical language such as “factory” or “barrel”\n- Stick to a common language profile, (tasks always being tasks, stages always being stages etc)\n- File structure should reflect the call stack\n- Use of JSDocs to explain variables in pure english\n- Include why things are done not just what is done\n- Use a labelled data inport pattern (IE  `({varA , varB}) => {}`)\n- NEVER MENTION DESIGN PATTERNS\n- Use @example tags in js doc to easily explain functionality\n  \n  \n\n## Functional over Object oreintated\n\nAlthough pure functional code can tend to insanity it is always important to note co-mingle state and functionality. Where possible state should leave in clearly defined places, and functions should show a clear line in how we move from one state to another. Traditional object oriented design mainly serves to gatekeep devs(or for game dev).\n\n### Principles\n\n- Try and avoid using classes where possible\n- Currying can be used to create sudo classes, avoid that\n- Functions should follow black box mentality, clear input delivers the same output with no side affects\n- Treat variables as immutable unless they are clearly defined states.\n- Functions should always be named with a verb in, as they are doing something\n- Give the miniumn data to each function as possible. Pick off fields before invocation.\n- Each function should only work to achieve its task, with a single responsibility\n\n\n## Co-location over abstraction\n\nAlthough abstraction is an essential part of coding it should always only be done by business level intent, not just on functionality. Ideally if you pick a random file in the codebase you should only need to look at the one folder above it and one folder under it to get all the context on its functionality.\n\n### Principles\n- Unit tests should always be placed next to the relevant file\n- Generally functions called in a higher function should be placed in a folder of that functions name. IE if `funA.js` calls `funB.js` it should be `./funA/funB.js`\n- Generic/helper functions should only be made if they are repeatedly doing the same thing.\n- Helpers should be treated like react state and exist at the lowest level folder that is common in the hierarchy of the folders\n- If abstracting it would take up more lines/characters than just embedding that line directly on a per file basis avoid doing it. IE don’t abstract a single line just because its repeated unless it has some complex logic like a regex.\n- Don’t fear repetition of code\n- Make sure the code is easily searchable for any given task. If I said modify the task history box in the ui it should  be easy and logical to figure out where that is.\n- Use folders as a tool for organising\n\n## Tested over trusted \n\nFunctionality should not assumed to exist until it is tested and evidenced. “it should work” isn’t always reliable and we want to make sure there are no regressions. \n\n### Principles\n- Try and at least plan what tests you are going to make before you  code a function\n- Don’t assume typing is correct until proven, or allow it to fail safe\n- Failures should clear transparent and observable, every function doesnt need to intensly check it just needs to report failures accurately\n- Tests must be consistent\n- Integration test must reflect how a user could want to use the app\n- Use the lowest possible level of tests( Ie Unit over api over e2e) for the fastest test cycle\n\n\n## Fast iteration over long planning\n\nSometimes you just can’t know what will happen without using it and that is essential. Spending too long planning can cause ideas to get confused or get you trapped in a loop where you just make plans worse.  Having simple clear checkpoints is great.\n\n### Principles\n- When planning, factor in points to check certain things and how the plan can be adapted when needed\n- Try and create safe ways to test functionality, ie not in prod, when possible as this will allow you to confirm things work.\n- Focus on one small change at a time, get tests passing then work on the next element.\n- Always design code with the intent it will be changed/replaced soon\n- Minimise friction in development even if it is small\n- Make change easy, then make the change. Even if making change easy is hard.\n\n\n\n# Inspirations\nMy principles here are inspired by:\n\n- Extreme programming Explained by Kent Beck (book)\n- Life isn’t binary (book)\n- Intent driven design by David whitney (Talk)\n\n\n# Examples\n\n## Intent Driven descriptions\n\n### Bad Example\n\n```js\n\nconst userInOneYearFactory = (name, age, users) => {\n\n    const user = {name: name , age: age + 1}\n\n    users.push(user)\n  \n}\n\nconst list = []\n\nuserFactory(\"Frank\",32,list)\n\n\n```\n\n## Good example\n\n```js\n\n/**\n* MARK: calculateAgeNextYear\n* @description calculates the age someone will be next year\n* @example const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: 3})  \nconsole.log(usersAgeNextYear) // 4\n*/\nconst calculateAgeNextYear = ({ageNow}) => {\n  const ageNextYear = ageNow + 1\n  \n  return ageNextYear\n}\n\nconst userObjectsList = []\n\nconst usersName = \"Frank\"\nconst usersAge = 32\n\nconst usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: usersAge})\n\nuserObjectsList.push({name: usersName, age: usersAge})\n\n\n```","isError":false,"durationMs":2,"source":"runner-structured","runnerId":"local-alpha","executionId":"6156eb89-ccbb-4d4d-9504-237933179721","seq":24},"fidelity":"normalized","seq":56,"blockId":"b16","tool":{"callId":"call_uc7qw8kr","name":"read","args":{"path":"docs/KB Code Standards.md","limit":2000},"result":"# Values\n\n## User understandable over technical language\n\nI feel like code should always be understandable by users as they are the ones who dictate process. Pick off fields before invocation.\\n- Each function should only work to achieve its task, with a single responsibility\\n\\n\\n## Co-location over abstraction\\n\\nAlthough abstraction is an essential part of coding it should always only be done by business level intent, not just on functionality. Ideally if you pick a random file in the codebase you should only need to look at the one folder above it and one folder under it to get all the context on its functionality.\\n\\n### Principles\\n- Unit tests should always be placed next to the relevant file\\n- Generally functions called in a higher function should be placed in a folder of that functions name. IE if `funA.js` calls `funB.js` it should be `./funA/funB.js`\\n- Generic/helper functions should only be made if they are repeatedly doing the same thing.\\n- Helpers should be treated like react state and exist at the lowest level folder that is common in the hierarchy of the folders\\n- If abstracting it would take up more lines/characters than just embedding that line directly on a per file basis avoid doing it. IE don’t abstract a single line just because its repeated unless it has some complex logic like a regex.\\n- Don’t fear repetition of code\\n- Make sure the code is easily searchable for any given task. If I said modify the task history box in the ui it should  be easy and logical to figure out where that is.\\n- Use folders as a tool for organising\\n\\n## Tested over trusted \\n\\nFunctionality should not assumed to exist until it is tested and evidenced. “it should work” isn’t always reliable and we want to make sure there are no regressions. \\n\\n### Principles\\n- Try and at least plan what tests you are going to make before you  code a function\\n- Don’t assume typing is correct until proven, or allow it to fail safe\\n- Failures should clear transparent and observable, every function doesnt need to intensly check it just needs to report failures accurately\\n- Tests must be consistent\\n- Integration test must reflect how a user could want to use the app\\n- Use the lowest possible level of tests( Ie Unit over api over e2e) for the fastest test cycle\\n\\n\\n## Fast iteration over long planning\\n\\nSometimes you just can’t know what will happen without using it and that is essential. Spending too long planning can cause ideas to get confused or get you trapped in a loop where you just make plans worse.  Having simple clear checkpoints is great.\\n\\n### Principles\\n- When planning, factor in points to check certain things and how the plan can be adapted when needed\\n- Try and create safe ways to test functionality, ie not in prod, when possible as this will allow you to confirm things work.\\n- Focus on one small change at a time, get tests passing then work on the next element.\\n- Always design code with the intent it will be changed/replaced soon\\n- Minimise friction in development even if it is small\\n- Make change easy, then make the change. Even if making change easy is hard.\\n\\n\\n\\n# Inspirations\\nMy principles here are inspired by:\\n\\n- Extreme programming Explained by Kent Beck (book)\\n- Life isn’t binary (book)\\n- Intent driven design by David whitney (Talk)\\n\\n\\n# Examples\\n\\n## Intent Driven descriptions\\n\\n### Bad Example\\n\\n```js\\n\\nconst userInOneYearFactory = (name, age, users) => {\\n\\n    const user = {name: name , age: age + 1}\\n\\n    users.push(user)\\n  \\n}\\n\\nconst list = []\\n\\nuserFactory(\\\"Frank\\\",32,list)\\n\\n\\n```\\n\\n## Good example\\n\\n```js\\n\\n/**\\n* MARK: calculateAgeNextYear\\n* @description calculates the age someone will be next year\\n* @example const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: 3})  \\nconsole.log(usersAgeNextYear) // 4\\n*/\\nconst calculateAgeNextYear = ({ageNow}) => {\\n  const ageNextYear = ageNow + 1\\n  \\n  return ageNextYear\\n}\\n\\nconst userObjectsList = []\\n\\nconst usersName = \\\"Frank\\\"\\nconst usersAge = 32\\n\\nconst usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: usersAge})\\n\\nuserObjectsList.push({name: usersName, age: Survey Decisions (Locked)\n10|\n11|| # | Question | Answer |\n12||---|----------|--------|\n13|| Q1 | Agent stage model in UI | Only the actual model the Runner serves (not the Runner default) |\n14|| Q2 | CI stage model field | No model / blank (CI uses no LLM) |\n15|| Q3 | Model source for reporting + dispatch | The exact model required by the dispatched task (`requirements.model`) |\n16|| Q4 | Task requires model Runner didn't advertise | Refuse assignment (leave for another Runner); alias: check other targets |\n17|| Q5 | Catalogue behaviours that must keep working | All five: picker non-empty, harness-specific lists correct, runnable/auth labels accurate, aliases resolve, dispatch matches available models |\n18|| Q6 | Model/harness pill while running (Runners view) | Yes, always while running |\n19|\n20|**Derived invariants:**\n21|\n22|- `config.model` / `config.models` is the Runner's **advertised capability** (what it _can_ run). It is never the stage's served model unless the stage happens to require that same model.\n23|- CI stages have no model; the Runner must not invent one for them (currently `config.model || \"default\"` leaks into CI posture/progress).\n24|- Alias resolution is already centralised (`resolveAliasRequirement`); the Runner must not second-guess it — dispatch hands it the concrete `requirements.model`.\n25|\n26|---\n27|\n28|## 2. Current Behaviour & Bug\n29|\n30|### 2.1 What the runner reports today\n31|\n32|`runner/daemon.js:executeAssignment` receives the dispatch answer's `requirements.model` as `model` and correctly passes it to `runHarnessStage({ model: model || config.model })` — the harness itself runs on the right model.\n33|\n34|But every **observable** path writes the Runner default instead:\n35|\n36|```js\n37|// daemon.js — progress \"prompted\" event\n38|model: config.model || \"default\"          // should be (kind === \"ci\" ? null : model || config.model || null)\n39|\n40|// daemon.js — complete (both CI pass/fail + agent)\n41|posture: `${tiers}:${harness}:${config.model || \"default\"}`   // should use the dispatch model\n42|\n43|// daemon.js — integration posture\n44|posture: `…:integration:${config.model || \"default\"}`        // integration has no LLM model either\n45|```\n46|\n47|The backend faithfully stores whatever the Runner sends (`executionLedger.recordProgress` → `stageServing`, `executionLedger.completeExecution` → `posture` history), and the frontend renders it (`PerRunnerTasksWidget` reads `assignment.serving.{harness,model}`; `MobileMonitorView` / `ActiveTaskPromptWidget` hide pills when `modelSelection` says so but otherwise show `serving.model`).\n48|\n49|Result: the UI perpetually shows the Runner's default (or literal `\"default\"`), never the stage's actual model; CI stages show a model they never used (the bug in the screenshot).\n50|\n51|### 2.2 Catalogue surface (must not regress)\n52|\n53|- `GET /compute/models` + `GET /harnesses/:id/models` served from `api/models.js` / `api/routes/compute.js` via `aggregateModelCatalog` / `getAvailableModels`, with `FALLBACK_MODELS` when discovery is empty.\n54|- `shared/modelKeys.js` grammar (canonical, re-exported by `api/models.js` + `frontend/src/services/api.js`) — parity pinned by `frontend/src/services/api.test.js`.\n55|- `api/aliasTargets.js` validates aliases against `modelIdsFor` (catalogue probe) + alias dispatch resolves centrally.\n56|- Frontend `ModelSelector.jsx` groups by harness, honours `modelSelection: \"list\" | \"none\"`, shows runnable/auth labels.\n57|- Dispatch matching (`runnerMatches` + `taskRequirements` + `resolveAliasRequirement`) must continue to match `requirements.model` against `capabilities.models`.\n58|\n59|---\n60|\n61|## 3. Guiding Principle: Make Change Easy, Then Make the Change\n62|\n63|The bug is a 3-line value error repeated in 4 places, but touching it safely requires:\n64|\n65|1. A single source of truth for \"what model does this assignment serve?\" so the fix cannot drift between the progress event, the posture string, and the harness call.\n66|2. A CI-blank contract that every downstream consumer agrees on.\n67|3. Tests that lock the corrected behaviour before the production code changes.\n68|\n69|Therefore **Phase 1** introduces the helper + fixtures + failing tests (no behaviour change to shipped code except the new helper). **Phase 2** rewires the four reporting sites to use it. **Phase 3** tightens dispatch refusal + catalogue regression tests.\n70|\n71|---\n72|\n73|## 4. Phase 1 — Make the Change Easy (No Behaviour Change to Shipped Reporting)\n74|\n75|### Step 1.1 — Introduce `servingModelFor` helper (single source of truth)\n76|\n77|- **File:** `runner/daemon.js` (or `runner/servingModel.js` if preferred — decide in review; keeping it in `daemon.js` avoids a new import graph)\n78|- **Signature:**\n79|\n80|  ```js\n81|  export function servingModelFor({ kind, model, fallbackModel } = {}) {}\n82|  ```\n83|\n84|- **Rules:**\n85|  - `kind === \"ci\" || kind === \"merge\" || kind === \"integrate\"` → `null` (no LLM; covers CI + merge/integrate which are also non-LLM).\n86|  - Otherwise → `model` when non-empty string, else `fallbackModel` when non-empty, else `null`.\n87|  - Never returns the string `\"default\"` — that literal is the bug. `null` means \"no model to report\".\n88|- **Why a helper:** without it the four call sites will be fixed by copy-pasted ternaries that re-diverge. One function is grep-able and test-able.\n89|- **Docs & parity:** mirror the comment on `taskRequirements` that CI stages are runnerless-model-less.\n90|\n91|### Step 1.2 — Add `servingModelFor` unit tests (failing → passing)\n92|\n93|- **File:** `runner/daemon.test.js` (extend)\n94|- **Cases:**\n95|  - agent with dispatch model → that model\n96|  - agent without dispatch model but with fallback → fallback\n97|  - agent with neither → null\n98|  - ci with any model → null (even if dispatch accidentally carries one)\n99|  - merge/integrate → null\n100|  - empty/whitespace model treated as absent\n101|\n102|### Step 1.3 — Introduce backend helper for posture formatting\n103|\n104|- **File:** `api/flow/executionLedger.js` or a small new `api/flow/runnerPosture.js`\n105|- **Fix:** `posture` currently `tiers:harness:model` where model is always present. For CI/integrate the model segment should be empty/omitted or explicitly blank so UI can hide the pill by contract. Decide: either omit trailing `:model` when null, or send `:`, with frontend already guarding `serving?.model` truthiness. Document the choice.\n106|- **Add helper:** `formatPosture({ tiers, harness, model })` → string, model segment absent when null.\n107|\n108|### Step 1.4 — Snapshot the current catalogue + dispatch test fixtures\n109|\n110|- Add/verify fixtures:\n111|  - `api/routes/compute.test.js` / `api/models.test.js` / `api/flow/dispatch/*.test.js` already pin catalogue + dispatch.\n112|  - Add a **regression test** in `api/flow/dispatch/runnerMatches.test.js` that a Runner advertising `[\"kimi-k3:cloud\"]` does NOT match a task requiring `gpt-oss:120b-cloud` (`NO_MODEL`), and that refusing that mismatch leaves the candidate for the next poll (the Q4 contract — the route already does this by `continue` on `!verdict.ok`, but the test locks it).\n113|  - Add a **catalogue smoke test**: `GET /compute/models` non-empty; `GET /harnesses/:id/models` for each harness returns only that harness's models; aliases resolve to real entries (covers Q5).\n114|\n115|---\n116|\n117|## 5. Phase 2 — Fix the Reporting (The Actual Change)\n118|\n119|### Step 2.1 — Wire `servingModelFor` into `executeAssignment` progress report\n120|\n121|- **File:** `runner/daemon.js`\n122|- **Change:**\n123|\n124|  ```js\n125|  const servingModel = servingModelFor({ kind, model, fallbackModel: config.model });\n126|  await client.progress({\n127|    stageId, event: \"prompted\", prompt,\n128|    harness: servingHarnessId,\n129|    model: servingModel, // null → omitted by client.progress body builder\n130|  });\n131|  ```\n132|\n133|- `runner/client.js:progress` already does `...(model ? { model } : {})` — null/empty omits the field, and `executionLedger.recordProgress` already guards `if (event === \"prompted\" && (harness || model))`. Verify CI now records `serving: { harness, model: null }` or no serving entry, not a fake model.\n134|\n135|### Step 2.2 — Wire into `complete` posture (all four sites)\n136|\n137|- **File:** `runner/daemon.js`\n138|- **Sites:**\n139|  1. CI pass `client.complete({ posture })`\n140|  2. CI fail `client.complete({ posture })`\n141|  3. Agent pass `client.complete({ posture })`\n142|  4. Agent fail (`err.failedOutcome`) `client.complete({ posture })`\n143|  5. Integration `posture` const\n144|- Use `formatPosture` + `servingModelFor` so CI/integration posture has no fake model segment.\n145|- Verify string never contains literal `\"default\"` unless a real model is literally named that.\n146|\n147|### Step 2.3 — Backend: store null cleanly + monitor omits blank model pill\n148|\n149|- **Files:** `api/flow/executionLedger.js`, `api/flow/runnerRoutes.js`\n150|- The monitor (`GET /runners/monitor`) joins `executionLedger.servingFor(executionId)` into `liveAssignments[].serving`. Ensure a `null` model stays `null` in the JSON (not `\"default\"` or `\"\"` that the UI might render).\n151|- **Frontend already correct:** `PerRunnerTasksWidget.jsx:287` guards `{serving?.model && ...}`; `ActiveTaskPromptWidget` hides model pill when `serving.model` falsy or `modelSelection === \"none\"`. Confirm no change needed; if needed, trim whitespace before check.\n152|\n153|### Step 2.4 — Runner advertise-vs-required model audit\n154|\n155|- **Files:** `runner/config.js` (`config.models`/`config.model`), `api/flow/dispatch/normalizeCapabilities.js`\n156|- Ensure Runner heartbeat `facts.models` is the advertised set; `runnerMatches` already checks `caps.models.includes(req.model)` and alias targets check availability. Document that `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODELS` (csv) is the operator's capability claim, not the stage model.\n157|- Add a log line when a dispatch `requirements.model` is not in `caps.models` is handled as `NO_MODEL` (already happens via `runnerMatches` → `misses.NO_MODEL` count in `runnerRoutes.js:dispatch`).\n158|\n159|---\n160|\n161|## 6. Phase 3 — Harden Dispatch Refusal + Catalogue Guarantees\n162|\n163|### Step 3.1 — Alias fallback: other targets from same alias\n164|\n165|- **File:** `api/flow/dispatch/resolveAliasRequirement.js` already re-resolves per dispatch poll; the Q4 note says \"if it is an alias it should look to see if any others from that alias are available\".\n166|- **Action:** Verify that when `resolveAliasRequirement` returns a target whose `model` the chosen Runner doesn't advertise, `runnerMatches` yields `NO_MODEL` → that candidate is skipped → next candidate (same task, same alias, but maybe a different Runner with a different target on re-resolve) is tried. Since resolution is weighted round-robin centralised, the natural re-resolve on next poll covers the \"try other alias targets\" case. Add a test that two Runners with disjoint model sets each pick different alias targets for the same alias.\n167|- If the current flow does NOT retry other targets within one dispatch poll, extend `runnerMatches` branching to, on `NO_MODEL` for an alias requirement, attempt the next weighted target before counting the miss. Keep this narrow — only for alias `req.alias` with `targetIndex`.\n168|\n169|### Step 3.2 — Catalogue regression sweep\n170|\n171|- **Files:** `api/models.js`, `shared/modelKeys.js`, `frontend/src/services/modelKeys.js`, `api/routes/compute.js`\n172|- **Test matrix (Q5 — all five):**\n173|  1. Model picker non-empty: `GET /compute/models` returns ≥1 entry (falls back to `FALLBACK_MODELS` when discovery empty).\n174|  2. Harness-specific lists correct: `GET /harnesses/:id/models` returns only that harness's models; unknown harness 404/empty, not cross-contamination.\n175|  3. Runnable/auth labels accurate: `withRunnableFlags` uses `providerAuthSummary` — test with mocked auth.\n176|  4. Aliases resolve to real catalogue entries: `validateAliasTargetModels` warns when model missing from target harness catalog; `sanitizeAliasTargetModels` strips malformed.\n177|  5. Runner dispatch matches available models: `runnerMatches` `NO_MODEL` vs `MATCH` table above.\n178|- Add a **parity test** for `shared/modelKeys.js` ↔ `api/models.js` key grammar if not already present (the architecture doc says one exists — verify it still passes).\n179|\n180|### Step 3.3 — Frontend Runners view always shows pill while running (Q6)\n181|\n182|- **File:** `frontend/src/components/observability/widgets/PerRunnerTasksWidget.jsx`\n183|- Already shows `serving.harness` + `serving.model` pills whenever truthy, on both full cards and compact rows. Verify compact `PerRunnerCompactRow` also surfaces `serving` (currently it doesn't — it shows only elapsed/task/stage; add harness/model pills there too if required by Q6 \"Yes, always while running\").\n184|- Add test: mock `getRunnerMonitor` with `serving: { harness: 'pi', model: 'kimi-k3:cloud' }` → pills visible on both compact and full variants.\n185|\n186|---\n187|\n188|## 7. Phase 4 — Testing & Verification Plan\n189|\n190|### 7.1 Unit tests (must pass before merge)\n191|\n192|| File | Covers |\n193||------|--------|\n194|| `runner/daemon.test.js` | `servingModelFor`, progress model null for CI, posture without default |\n195|| `runner/client.test.js` | `progress({ model: null })` omits field; `progress({ model: \"x\" })` sends it |\n196|| `api/flow/executionLedger.test.js` | `recordProgress` stores null model; `servingFor` returns null; `completeExecution` history without fake model |\n197|| `api/flow/dispatch/runnerMatches.test.js` | `NO_MODEL` vs `MATCH`, alias retry |\n198|| `api/flow/dispatch/taskRequirements.test.js` | CI kind has no model/harness, agent has model |\n199|| `api/flow/runnerRoutes.test.js` | Dispatch refuses NO_MODEL, monitor omits blank model pill |\n200|| `frontend/.../PerRunnerTasksWidget.test.jsx` | Pills show actual model, hidden for CI, visible while running |\n201|| `frontend/.../MobileMonitorView.test.jsx` | Scripted stages render \"Automated — no model\" |\n202|| `api/models.test.js` / `api/routes/compute.test.js` | Catalogue non-empty, harness-scoped, runnable labels, aliases |\n203|\n204|### 7.2 Commands\n205|\n206|```bash\n207|npm run test:unit                          # entire suite — gate for the stage\n208|npm run test:frontend -- PerRunnerTasksWidget\n209|npm run test:frontend -- MobileMonitorView\n210|npm run lint\n211|# Optional: headless screenshot of Runners view with seeded monitor data\n212|npm run capture:screenshot\n213|```\n214|\n215|### 7.3 Manual / smoke verification (no long-lived servers)\n216|\n217|- Seed a project with one `agent` stage (model `kimi-k3:cloud`) and one `ci` stage (`npm test`).\n218|- Start a Runner with `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODELS=kimi-k3:cloud,gpt-oss:120b-cloud` and observe:\n219|  - Monitor shows `kimi-k3:cloud` on the agent card, no model pill on the CI card.\n220|  - Posture history line for CI has no fake `default` segment.\n221|- Start a second Runner advertising only `gpt-oss:120b-cloud`; dispatch an agent requiring `kimi-k3:cloud` — only the first Runner should match (Q4).\n222|\n223|---\n224|\n225|## 8. Risks & Mitigations\n226|\n227|| Risk | Mitigation |\n228||------|------------|\n229|| Posture string consumers parse it assuming 3 segments | Keep `tiers:harness:model` shape; when model is null either omit last segment or emit empty — document and update parsers; add migration note |\n230|| `config.model` empty string regressions | Helper treats `\"\"` / whitespace as absent → null, never `\"default\"` |\n231|| Alias alias-model mismatch counted as miss forever | Central re-resolve on next poll rotates to another target automatically; test two-Runner disjoint case |\n232|| Frontend pills flicker on prompt delay | `executionLedger.stageServing` is set on `prompted` progress; until then `serving` is null and pills are hidden — acceptable (same as today) |\n233|| Integration/merge stages accidentally show model | Helper classifies `kind === \"merge\"` / `\"integrate\"` as non-LLM |\n234|\n235|---\n236|\n237|## 9. Documentation & Follow-up\n238|\n239|- Update `docs/KB Architecture.md` Runner section: explain advertised `models` vs dispatched `requirements.model` vs `serving.model` vs `posture` model segment.\n240|- Update operator docs (`KB Local Integration details.md` or Runner README) for `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODELS` / `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODEL` semantics.\n241|- Add ADR or inline comment linking `servingModelFor` to this plan + SURVEY.md.\n242|\n243|---\n244|\n245|## 10. Sequencing Summary\n246|\n247|1. **Phase 1 first** (biggest research, lowest risk): helper + tests + catalogue snapshots.\n248|2. **Phase 2** (the fix): 4-site rewire — small diff, high confidence because Phase 1 tests already assert it.\n249|3. **Phase 3** (hardening): alias retry + catalogue matrix + Q6 pill-always.\n250|4. **Phase 4**: run the gates, manual smoke, screenshot evidence, doc CI stages run a command, not an\n13| *      LLM, so inventing a model for them is a lie the UI would render.\n14| *   2. Otherwise the dispatched task's required model wins (`model`).\n15| *   3. Vitest's DEFAULT coverage `exclude`\\n\\t\\t// already drops `*.test.js`/node_modules — restating `exclude`\\n\\t\\t// here would REPLACE those defaults, so do not add one.\\n\\t\\t// Raw output lands in `./coverage/` (gitignored); the committed\\n\\t\\t// baseline copy lives in `docs/baseline/WP-1-coverage.*`.\\n\\t\\tcoverage: {\\n\\t\\t\\tprovider: \\\"v8\\\",\\n\\t\\t\\treporter: [\\\"json-summary\\\", \\\"text\\\", \\\"html\\\"],\\n\\t\\t\\treportsDirectory: \\\"./coverage\\\",\\n\\t\\t\\tinclude: [\\\"work/**\\\", \\\"flow/**\\\", \\\"house/**\\\", \\\"git/**\\\", `${SHARED_DIR}/**`],\\n\\t\\t\\tallowExternal: true,\\n\\t\\t\\t// MARK: core-module coverage gate (WP-8: exactly three gates)\\n\\t\\t\\t// Fixed floor: every measured core module (api/work, api/flow,\\n\\t\\t\\t// api/house, api/git, shared) must hold >=70% lines, enforced\\n\\t\\t\\t// per file so one thin module cannot hide behind a hot barrel.\\n\\t\\t\\t// Reproduce locally with `npm run test:coverage` (root or api).\\n\\t\\t\\tthresholds: { lines: 70, perFile: true },\\n\\t\\t},\\n\\t\\ttestTimeout: 120000,\\n\\t\\t// MARK: hookTimeout matches testTimeout (deploy-gate flake, 2026-10-05).\\n\\t\\t// Under the overlapped gate (api + frontend + lint + build + canary\\n\\t\\t// sharing 4 cores with 246 vitest workers), import, server boot, and\\n\\t\\t// integration test paths can stretch past 60s under peak CPU contention;\\n\\t\\t// 120s provides an honest safety margin so real regressions fail loudly\\n\\t\\t// while scheduling starvation does not flake the gate.\\n\\t\\thookTimeout: 120000,\\n\\t\\tinclude: [\\\"**/*.test.js\\\"],\\n\\t\\t// MARK: NODE_ENV pin (TEST ENV CONTRACT, api/sessionStore.js)\\n\\t\\t// The api test suite runs on the mock session harness, which the\\n\\t\\t// sessionStore engages by reading NODE_ENV at module-import time. Vitest\\n\\t\\t// only *defaults* NODE_ENV to \\\"test\\\" when it is unset, so an inherited\\n\\t\\t// value (e.g. NODE_ENV=production from a deployed service shell or CI\\n\\t\\t// runner) would silently disengage the seam and spin up REAL pi agent\\n\\t\\t// sessions. Setting it here overrides any inherited value, making the\\n\\t\\t// suite hermetic in every environment. `api/testEnvGuard.test.js` fails\\n\\t\\t// loudly if this pin ever stops landing before module import.\\n\\t\\tenv: {\\n\\t\\tNODE_ENV: \\\"test\\\",\\n\\t\\t// MARK: gate-tolerant agy discovery watchdog (same seam philosophy as\\n\\t\\t// the AGY bin pin below). Under the overlapped `npm test` gate the api\\n\\t\\t// suite shares 4 cores with ~10 other branches; a spawned mock-agy\\n\\t\\t// child can take far longer than the 15s production watchdog to be\\n\\t\\t// scheduled and exit, which would misclassify a healthy CLI as\\n\\t\\t// AGY_MODELS_TIMEOUT and flake discovery-path assertions. 60s keeps\\n\\t\\t// real hangs loud (well under vitest's 90s testTimeout) while\\n\\t\\t// scheduling starvation no longer flakes the gate. Production keeps\\n\\t\\t// the 15s default.\\n\\t\\tKAINBAIN_AGY_MODELS_TIMEOUT_MS: \\\"60s\\\",\\n\\t\\t\\t// MARK: hermetic agy CLI (same seam philosophy as the NODE_ENV pin).\\n\\t\\t\\t// The antigravity harness's model discovery spawns `config.agyBin`\\n\\t\\t\\t// (default \\\"agy\\\") whenever the model cache is bypassed, so every\\n\\t\\t\\t// `?refresh=true` listing through /compute/models and\\n\\t\\t\\t// /harnesses/:id/models would otherwise pay a REAL CLI spawn per test\\n\\t\\t\\t// when agy is installed on the host (~2s each — the api suite's\\n\\t\\t\\t// dominant wall-time source) and the route tests would behave\\n\\t\\t\\t// differently on hosts with vs without the CLI. Pinning it to the\\n\\t\\t\\t// repo's deterministic fixture mock (~35ms, no network, same wire\\n\\t\\t\\t// output the antigravity suites already assert against) keeps those\\n\\t\\t\\t// route tests hermetic and fast everywhere. Pinning the exec transport keeps\\n\\t\\t\\t// the suite hermetic and identical everywhere; the MSP path has\\n\\t\\t\\t// dedicated mock-host coverage in\\n\\t\\t\\t//
